challenges.answer: CREATE TEMP TABLE integrated_customers AS WITH crm AS(WITH ranked AS (SELECT *,ROW_NUMBER() OVER(PARTITION BY TRIM(customer_id) ORDER BY updated_at DESC,source_row DESC) AS rn FROM crm_people WHERE customer_id IS NOT NULL AND TRIM(customer_id)<>'') SELECT TRIM(customer_id) AS customer_id,TRIM(name) AS name,CASE UPPER(TRIM(gender)) WHEN 'F' THEN 'Female' WHEN 'M' THEN 'Male' ELSE NULL END AS crm_gender FROM ranked WHERE rn=1),erp AS(SELECT CASE WHEN SUBSTR(TRIM(erp_id),1,3)='NAS' THEN SUBSTR(TRIM(erp_id),4) ELSE TRIM(erp_id) END AS customer_id,CASE UPPER(TRIM(gender)) WHEN 'F' THEN 'Female' WHEN 'FEMALE' THEN 'Female' WHEN 'M' THEN 'Male' WHEN 'MALE' THEN 'Male' ELSE NULL END AS erp_gender,birth_date FROM erp_people),loc AS(SELECT REPLACE(TRIM(erp_id),'-','') AS customer_id,CASE UPPER(TRIM(country_code)) WHEN 'US' THEN 'United States' WHEN 'USA' THEN 'United States' WHEN 'GB' THEN 'United Kingdom' WHEN 'UK' THEN 'United Kingdom' WHEN 'IND' THEN 'India' ELSE 'Unknown' END AS country FROM erp_locations) SELECT c.customer_id,c.name,COALESCE(c.crm_gender,e.erp_gender,'Unknown') AS gender,COALESCE(l.country,'Unknown') AS country,CASE WHEN e.birth_date GLOB '[0-9][0-9][0-9][0-9]-[0-9][0-9]-[0-9][0-9]' AND date(e.birth_date,'+0 days')=e.birth_date AND e.birth_date<='2025-04-01' THEN e.birth_date ELSE NULL END AS birth_date FROM crm c LEFT JOIN erp e ON e.customer_id=c.customer_id LEFT JOIN loc l ON l.customer_id=c.customer_id; CREATE TEMP TABLE built_sales AS SELECT b.row_id AS sale_key,c.customer_key,p.product_key,CAST(b.quantity AS INTEGER) AS quantity,CAST(b.quantity AS INTEGER)*p.price AS sales,b.order_date FROM bronze_sales b JOIN dim_customer c ON c.customer_id=TRIM(b.customer_id) JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_id=TRIM(b.product_id) WHERE TRIM(b.quantity)<>'' AND TRIM(b.quantity) NOT GLOB '*[^0-9]*' AND CAST(b.quantity AS INTEGER)>0 AND b.order_date GLOB '[0-9][0-9][0-9][0-9]-[0-9][0-9]-[0-9][0-9]' AND date(b.order_date,'+0 days')=b.order_date; SELECT i.country,COALESCE(SUM(s.sales),0) AS total_sales FROM integrated_customers i JOIN dim_customer c ON c.customer_id=i.customer_id LEFT JOIN built_sales s ON s.customer_key=c.customer_key GROUP BY i.country

questions.title: Meet your first SELECT · Challenge 1
questions.prompt: Show the name and city of every customer.
questions.rationale: Two projections reinforce column selection before filters; small customer and product schemas remain appropriate.
questions.solution: SELECT name, city FROM store_customers

questions.title: Meet your first SELECT · Challenge 2
questions.prompt: Show the name and price of every product.
questions.rationale: Two projections reinforce column selection before filters; small customer and product schemas remain appropriate.
questions.solution: SELECT name, price FROM store_products

questions.title: Aliases & calculated columns · Challenge 1
questions.prompt: Return name and price * 2 as double_price for every product.
questions.rationale: Transfers a calculated alias from money to quantity without introducing aggregation; quiz distinguishes output from mutation.
questions.solution: SELECT name, price*2 AS double_price FROM store_products

questions.title: Aliases & calculated columns · Challenge 2
questions.prompt: Return id and quantity * 10 as units_times_ten for every order.
questions.rationale: Transfers a calculated alias from money to quantity without introducing aggregation; quiz distinguishes output from mutation.
questions.solution: SELECT id, quantity*10 AS units_times_ten FROM store_orders

questions.title: Filter with WHERE · Challenge 1
questions.prompt: Show name and city for store_customers in Chicago.
questions.rationale: Replaces a second city-equality task with status filtering on purchase lines; changes the row grain without a syntax jump.
questions.solution: SELECT name,city FROM store_customers WHERE city='Chicago'

questions.title: Filter with WHERE · Challenge 2
questions.prompt: Show id and quantity for cancelled purchase lines in store_orders.
questions.rationale: Replaces a second city-equality task with status filtering on purchase lines; changes the row grain without a syntax jump.
questions.solution: SELECT id,quantity FROM store_orders WHERE status='cancelled'

questions.title: Comparisons & ranges · Challenge 1
questions.prompt: Show name and price for store_products priced at least 45.
questions.rationale: Single lower bound transfers to an inclusive two-sided range; exact endpoints matter.
questions.solution: SELECT name,price FROM store_products WHERE price>=45

questions.title: Comparisons & ranges · Challenge 2
questions.prompt: Show name and price for store_products priced between 12 and 80 inclusive.
questions.rationale: Single lower bound transfers to an inclusive two-sided range; exact endpoints matter.
questions.solution: SELECT name,price FROM store_products WHERE price BETWEEN 12 AND 80

questions.title: Combine conditions · Challenge 1
questions.prompt: Show name and price for Tech store_products costing less than 100.
questions.rationale: Conjunction transfers to a grouped disjunction; parentheses and precedence add useful reasoning.
questions.solution: SELECT name,price FROM store_products WHERE category='Tech' AND price<100

questions.title: Combine conditions · Challenge 2
questions.prompt: Show name and price for Home or Stationery store_products costing at least 12.
questions.rationale: Conjunction transfers to a grouped disjunction; parentheses and precedence add useful reasoning.
questions.solution: SELECT name,price FROM store_products WHERE (category='Home' OR category='Stationery') AND price>=12

questions.title: Lists & text patterns · Challenge 1
questions.prompt: Show name for store_customers whose name starts with A.
questions.rationale: Prefix matching transfers to an explicit membership list; neither requires joins.
questions.solution: SELECT name FROM store_customers WHERE name LIKE 'A%'

questions.title: Lists & text patterns · Challenge 2
questions.prompt: Show name and city for store_customers in Austin or Seattle.
questions.rationale: Prefix matching transfers to an explicit membership list; neither requires joins.
questions.solution: SELECT name,city FROM store_customers WHERE city IN ('Austin','Seattle')

questions.title: Understand NULL · Challenge 1
questions.prompt: Show name for store_customers whose city is missing.
questions.rationale: Detection of missing values transfers to display fallback; quiz checks UNKNOWN rather than treating NULL as text.
questions.solution: SELECT name FROM store_customers WHERE city IS NULL

questions.title: Understand NULL · Challenge 2
questions.prompt: Return name and city, replacing missing city with Unknown (alias the column city).
questions.rationale: Detection of missing values transfers to display fallback; quiz checks UNKNOWN rather than treating NULL as text.
questions.solution: SELECT name,COALESCE(city,'Unknown') AS city FROM store_customers

questions.title: Sort & limit · Challenge 1
questions.prompt: Show name and price of the 3 most expensive store_products, highest price first.
questions.rationale: Descending and ascending limits are intentional early repetition; the quiz introduces deterministic tie-breaking.
questions.solution: SELECT name,price FROM store_products ORDER BY price DESC LIMIT 3

questions.title: Sort & limit · Challenge 2
questions.prompt: Show name and price of the 2 cheapest store_products, lowest price first.
questions.rationale: Descending and ascending limits are intentional early repetition; the quiz introduces deterministic tie-breaking.
questions.solution: SELECT name,price FROM store_products ORDER BY price ASC LIMIT 2

questions.title: Unique values with DISTINCT · Challenge 1
questions.prompt: Show each distinct customer city, including NULL.
questions.rationale: City NULL versus category values reinforces distinctness on two small columns.
questions.solution: SELECT DISTINCT city FROM store_customers

questions.title: Unique values with DISTINCT · Challenge 2
questions.prompt: Show each distinct product category.
questions.rationale: City NULL versus category values reinforces distinctness on two small columns.
questions.solution: SELECT DISTINCT category FROM store_products

questions.title: COUNT, SUM & AVG · Challenge 1
questions.prompt: Return the number of store_customers as customer_count.
questions.rationale: Row count transfers to quantity sum; quiz separates COUNT(*) from COUNT(nullable_column).
questions.solution: SELECT COUNT(*) AS customer_count FROM store_customers

questions.title: COUNT, SUM & AVG · Challenge 2
questions.prompt: Return total order quantity as total_units.
questions.rationale: Row count transfers to quantity sum; quiz separates COUNT(*) from COUNT(nullable_column).
questions.solution: SELECT SUM(quantity) AS total_units FROM store_orders

questions.title: Group into summaries · Challenge 1
questions.prompt: Show category and product_count for each product category.
questions.rationale: Category counts transfer to status totals; both explicitly change the result grain.
questions.solution: SELECT category,COUNT(*) AS product_count FROM store_products GROUP BY category

questions.title: Group into summaries · Challenge 2
questions.prompt: Show status and total_units (sum of quantity) for each order status.
questions.rationale: Category counts transfer to status totals; both explicitly change the result grain.
questions.solution: SELECT status,SUM(quantity) AS total_units FROM store_orders GROUP BY status

questions.title: MIN, MAX & the grain of a result · Challenge 1
questions.prompt: Return shortest_watch and longest_watch: minimum and maximum watch_seconds across all watch events.
questions.rationale: Global MIN/MAX transfers to grouped maxima; quiz checks the one-row global summary grain.
questions.solution: SELECT MIN(watch_seconds) AS shortest_watch,MAX(watch_seconds) AS longest_watch FROM watch_events

questions.title: MIN, MAX & the grain of a result · Challenge 2
questions.prompt: Return video_id and longest_watch: maximum watch_seconds for each video that has events.
questions.rationale: Global MIN/MAX transfers to grouped maxima; quiz checks the one-row global summary grain.
questions.solution: SELECT video_id,MAX(watch_seconds) AS longest_watch FROM watch_events GROUP BY video_id

questions.title: Filter groups with HAVING · Challenge 1
questions.prompt: Show customer_id and order_count for store_customers with at least 2 store_orders.
questions.rationale: Count-based HAVING transfers to a quantity threshold; filtering groups is the common concept.
questions.solution: SELECT customer_id,COUNT(*) AS order_count FROM store_orders GROUP BY customer_id HAVING COUNT(*)>=2

questions.title: Filter groups with HAVING · Challenge 2
questions.prompt: Show customer_id and total_units for store_customers with total quantity greater than 3.
questions.rationale: Count-based HAVING transfers to a quantity threshold; filtering groups is the common concept.
questions.solution: SELECT customer_id,SUM(quantity) AS total_units FROM store_orders GROUP BY customer_id HAVING SUM(quantity)>3

questions.title: Make decisions with CASE · Challenge 1
questions.prompt: Show name and tier: Premium if price >= 80, otherwise Standard.
questions.rationale: Text classification transfers to a numeric indicator; ELSE and equality boundaries are explicit.
questions.solution: SELECT name,CASE WHEN price>=80 THEN 'Premium' ELSE 'Standard' END AS tier FROM store_products

questions.title: Make decisions with CASE · Challenge 2
questions.prompt: Show id and is_paid: 1 for paid store_orders, otherwise 0.
questions.rationale: Text classification transfers to a numeric indicator; ELSE and equality boundaries are explicit.
questions.solution: SELECT id,CASE WHEN status='paid' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_paid FROM store_orders

questions.title: Conditional aggregation · Challenge 1
questions.prompt: Return wet_observations: the number of daily_weather rows with element PRCP, raw_value greater than zero and no quality_flag. A missing value does not count as wet.
questions.rationale: Weather count transfers to conditional Celsius averaging; missing/flagged values must not become zero.
questions.solution: SELECT SUM(CASE WHEN element='PRCP' AND raw_value>0 AND quality_flag IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS wet_observations FROM daily_weather

questions.title: Conditional aggregation · Challenge 2
questions.prompt: For every station_id present in daily_weather, return station_id and avg_tmax_c: the average usable TMAX in Celsius, rounded to two decimals. A usable value has quality_flag NULL and raw_value non-NULL. Divide raw tenths by 10.0. Preserve NULL if no usable TMAX exists; do not average other elements as zeros.
questions.rationale: Weather count transfers to conditional Celsius averaging; missing/flagged values must not become zero.
questions.solution: SELECT station_id,ROUND(AVG(CASE WHEN element='TMAX' AND quality_flag IS NULL THEN raw_value/10.0 END),2) AS avg_tmax_c FROM daily_weather GROUP BY station_id

questions.title: CAST & numeric measurements · Challenge 1
questions.prompt: Return device_id, observed_at and temperature_text by casting temperature_c to TEXT for every sensor reading.
questions.rationale: Sensor CAST transfers to numeric deviation with Celsius units; quiz now warns that coercion is not validation.
questions.solution: SELECT device_id,observed_at,CAST(temperature_c AS TEXT) AS temperature_text FROM sensor_readings

questions.title: CAST & numeric measurements · Challenge 2
questions.prompt: Return device_id, observed_at and deviation_c: absolute difference between temperature_c and 20.0 Celsius, rounded to two decimals.
questions.rationale: Sensor CAST transfers to numeric deviation with Celsius units; quiz now warns that coercion is not validation.
questions.solution: SELECT device_id,observed_at,ROUND(ABS(temperature_c-20.0),2) AS deviation_c FROM sensor_readings

questions.title: Databases, schemas, tables & keys · Challenge 1
questions.prompt: Return name and type for the store_customers, store_products and store_orders tables from sqlite_schema.
questions.rationale: Schema inspection transfers to a real key-based join; canonical table names now agree with sqlite_schema.
questions.solution: SELECT name,type FROM sqlite_schema WHERE type='table' AND name IN('store_customers','store_products','store_orders')

questions.title: Databases, schemas, tables & keys · Challenge 2
questions.prompt: Return order_id and customer_name by joining store_orders.customer_id to store_customers.id for every order.
questions.rationale: Schema inspection transfers to a real key-based join; canonical table names now agree with sqlite_schema.
questions.solution: SELECT o.id AS order_id,c.name AS customer_name FROM store_orders o JOIN store_customers c ON c.id=o.customer_id

questions.title: Connect tables with JOIN · Challenge 1
questions.prompt: Return every order id and its customer name (columns id, name).
questions.rationale: Two foreign-key joins intentionally reinforce relationship direction before outer joins.
questions.solution: SELECT o.id,c.name FROM store_orders o JOIN store_customers c ON c.id=o.customer_id

questions.title: Connect tables with JOIN · Challenge 2
questions.prompt: Return every order id and its product name (columns id, name).
questions.rationale: Two foreign-key joins intentionally reinforce relationship direction before outer joins.
questions.solution: SELECT o.id,p.name FROM store_orders o JOIN store_products p ON p.id=o.product_id

questions.title: Keep unmatched rows · Challenge 1
questions.prompt: Show every customer name and order_count, including store_customers with zero store_orders.
questions.rationale: Preserving all customers transfers to selecting only unmatched customers; COUNT(key) is essential.
questions.solution: SELECT c.name,COUNT(o.id) AS order_count FROM store_customers c LEFT JOIN store_orders o ON o.customer_id=c.id GROUP BY c.id,c.name

questions.title: Keep unmatched rows · Challenge 2
questions.prompt: Show name for store_customers with no store_orders.
questions.rationale: Preserving all customers transfers to selecting only unmatched customers; COUNT(key) is essential.
questions.solution: SELECT c.name FROM store_customers c LEFT JOIN store_orders o ON o.customer_id=c.id WHERE o.id IS NULL

questions.title: Ratios, ROUND & NULLIF · Challenge 1
questions.prompt: Return account_id and success_pct (0–100, rounded to 2 decimals) for accounts with requests.
questions.rationale: Observed-account rates transfer to the full account population; no-request denominators remain NULL.
questions.solution: SELECT account_id,ROUND(100.0*SUM(CASE WHEN status='success' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)/NULLIF(COUNT(*),0),2) AS success_pct FROM ai_requests GROUP BY account_id

questions.title: Ratios, ROUND & NULLIF · Challenge 2
questions.difficultyWhy: Reviewed (rubric said hard, score 6): LEFT JOIN + NULLIF ratio; several features but one clear idea.
questions.prompt: Return id and success_pct for every account, including accounts with no requests (NULL rate). Round to 2 decimals.
questions.rationale: Observed-account rates transfer to the full account population; no-request denominators remain NULL.
questions.solution: SELECT a.id,ROUND(100.0*SUM(CASE WHEN r.status='success' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)/NULLIF(COUNT(r.id),0),2) AS success_pct FROM ai_accounts a LEFT JOIN ai_requests r ON r.account_id=a.id GROUP BY a.id

questions.title: Revenue across tables · Challenge 1
questions.prompt: Show customer name and paid revenue (alias revenue), only store_customers with paid store_orders.
questions.rationale: Customer revenue transfers to category revenue; purchase-line grain is stated and price multiplication precedes aggregation.
questions.solution: SELECT c.name,SUM(o.quantity*p.price) AS revenue FROM store_orders o JOIN store_customers c ON c.id=o.customer_id JOIN store_products p ON p.id=o.product_id WHERE o.status='paid' GROUP BY c.id,c.name

questions.title: Revenue across tables · Challenge 2
questions.prompt: Show category and paid revenue (alias revenue) for each category with paid store_orders.
questions.rationale: Customer revenue transfers to category revenue; purchase-line grain is stated and price multiplication precedes aggregation.
questions.solution: SELECT p.category,SUM(o.quantity*p.price) AS revenue FROM store_orders o JOIN store_products p ON p.id=o.product_id WHERE o.status='paid' GROUP BY p.category

questions.title: Self-joins & manager relationships · Challenge 1
questions.prompt: Return employee_id and manager_name for every employee, preserving NULL manager_name when manager_id has no match.
questions.rationale: Developer manager roles replace referral labels; transfer compares employee and direct-manager salaries after joining.
questions.solution: SELECT e.id AS employee_id,m.name AS manager_name FROM employees e LEFT JOIN employees m ON m.id=e.manager_id

questions.title: Self-joins & manager relationships · Challenge 2
questions.prompt: Return employee_id and manager_id for employees whose salary is greater than their direct manager’s salary. Exclude employees without a manager.
questions.rationale: Developer manager roles replace referral labels; transfer compares employee and direct-manager salaries after joining.
questions.solution: SELECT e.id AS employee_id,m.id AS manager_id FROM employees e JOIN employees m ON m.id=e.manager_id WHERE e.salary>m.salary

questions.title: CROSS JOIN & a complete date grid · Challenge 1
questions.difficultyWhy: Reviewed (rubric said easy, score 2.5): Fixed VALUES date list plus CROSS JOIN; mechanical once the date source is given.
questions.prompt: Return day and viewer_id for every day from 2025-01-01 through 2025-01-03 inclusive and every viewer, including pre-signup combinations.
questions.rationale: A provided date list teaches Cartesian grids before recursion; challenge 2 adds signup eligibility and stays lesson-only.
questions.solution: SELECT day,v.id AS viewer_id FROM (SELECT column1 AS day FROM (VALUES ('2025-01-01'), ('2025-01-02'), ('2025-01-03'))) AS days CROSS JOIN viewers v

questions.title: CROSS JOIN & a complete date grid · Challenge 2
questions.difficultyWhy: Reviewed (rubric said easy, score 2.5): Same date-grid pattern with one signup filter.
questions.prompt: Return day and viewer_id for the same date range, keeping only combinations on or after that viewer's signup_at.
questions.rationale: A provided date list teaches Cartesian grids before recursion; challenge 2 adds signup eligibility and stays lesson-only.
questions.solution: SELECT day,v.id AS viewer_id FROM (SELECT column1 AS day FROM (VALUES ('2025-01-01'), ('2025-01-02'), ('2025-01-03'))) AS days CROSS JOIN viewers v WHERE day>=v.signup_at

questions.title: FULL OUTER JOIN & unmatched records · Challenge 1
questions.prompt: Return invoice_id and payment_id for every invoice/payment match, retaining unmatched rows on either side. Keep split invoice_payments as separate rows.
questions.rationale: Matched and unmatched invoice/payment rows transfer to orphan detection; split payments remain separate rows.
questions.solution: SELECT i.id AS invoice_id,p.id AS payment_id FROM invoices i FULL OUTER JOIN invoice_payments p ON p.invoice_id=i.id

questions.title: FULL OUTER JOIN & unmatched records · Challenge 2
questions.prompt: Return payment_id for invoice_payments whose invoice_id has no matching invoice, including NULL invoice_id.
questions.rationale: Matched and unmatched invoice/payment rows transfer to orphan detection; split payments remain separate rows.
questions.solution: SELECT p.id AS payment_id FROM invoice_payments p LEFT JOIN invoices i ON i.id=p.invoice_id WHERE i.id IS NULL

questions.title: ON versus WHERE in a LEFT JOIN · Challenge 1
questions.prompt: Return provider_id and completed_visits for every provider. Include zero for providers with no completed encounter.
questions.rationale: Healthcare provider counts transfer to the registered-patient denominator; ON filtering and COUNT(key) preserve zero groups.
questions.solution: SELECT p.id AS provider_id,COUNT(e.id) AS completed_visits FROM providers p LEFT JOIN encounters e ON e.provider_id=p.id AND e.status='completed' GROUP BY p.id

questions.title: ON versus WHERE in a LEFT JOIN · Challenge 2
questions.prompt: Return patient_id and cancelled_visits for every patient. Count only cancelled encounters, retaining patients with no cancelled encounters as zero.
questions.rationale: Healthcare provider counts transfer to the registered-patient denominator; ON filtering and COUNT(key) preserve zero groups.
questions.solution: SELECT p.id AS patient_id,COUNT(e.id) AS cancelled_visits FROM patients p LEFT JOIN encounters e ON e.patient_id=p.id AND e.status='cancelled' GROUP BY p.id

questions.title: Combine sets with UNION · Challenge 1
questions.prompt: Return distinct city values from Chicago store_customers and Austin store_customers using UNION.
questions.rationale: UNION versus UNION ALL intentionally contrast set and bag behavior; duplicates are the transfer edge case.
questions.solution: SELECT city FROM store_customers WHERE city='Chicago' UNION SELECT city FROM store_customers WHERE city='Austin'

questions.title: Combine sets with UNION · Challenge 2
questions.prompt: Stack name from store_customers and name from store_products, keeping duplicates.
questions.rationale: UNION versus UNION ALL intentionally contrast set and bag behavior; duplicates are the transfer edge case.
questions.solution: SELECT name FROM store_customers UNION ALL SELECT name FROM store_products

questions.title: INTERSECT & EXCEPT · Challenge 1
questions.prompt: Return viewer_id for viewers who watched both video 1 and video 2. Each viewer appears once.
questions.rationale: INTERSECT and EXCEPT contrast shared membership with one-sided exclusion; each output is distinct.
questions.solution: SELECT viewer_id FROM watch_events WHERE video_id=1 INTERSECT SELECT viewer_id FROM watch_events WHERE video_id=2

questions.title: INTERSECT & EXCEPT · Challenge 2
questions.prompt: Return viewer_id for viewers who watched video 1 but never video 2. Each viewer appears once.
questions.rationale: INTERSECT and EXCEPT contrast shared membership with one-sided exclusion; each output is distinct.
questions.solution: SELECT viewer_id FROM watch_events WHERE video_id=1 EXCEPT SELECT viewer_id FROM watch_events WHERE video_id=2

questions.title: Subqueries · Challenge 1
questions.prompt: Return name and price for store_products priced above the overall average product price.
questions.rationale: Replaces a second overall average with an own-category correlated benchmark; explanation and quiz now teach correlation.
questions.solution: SELECT name,price FROM store_products WHERE price>(SELECT AVG(price) FROM store_products)

questions.title: Subqueries · Challenge 2
questions.prompt: Return name and price for store_products priced above the average price in their own category. A product equal to its category average does not qualify.
questions.rationale: Replaces a second overall average with an own-category correlated benchmark; explanation and quiz now teach correlation.
questions.solution: SELECT p.name,p.price FROM store_products p WHERE p.price>(SELECT AVG(x.price) FROM store_products x WHERE x.category=p.category)

questions.title: Ask whether a row exists · Challenge 1
questions.prompt: Show name of store_customers who have at least one paid order.
questions.rationale: EXISTS versus NOT EXISTS intentionally contrast positive and negative quantification without fan-out.
questions.solution: SELECT c.name FROM store_customers c WHERE EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM store_orders o WHERE o.customer_id=c.id AND o.status='paid')

questions.title: Ask whether a row exists · Challenge 2
questions.prompt: Show name of store_customers who have no paid store_orders.
questions.rationale: EXISTS versus NOT EXISTS intentionally contrast positive and negative quantification without fan-out.
questions.solution: SELECT c.name FROM store_customers c WHERE NOT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM store_orders o WHERE o.customer_id=c.id AND o.status='paid')

questions.title: NOT IN and the NULL trap · Challenge 1
questions.prompt: Return id for viewers who have not referred anyone. A referred_by value identifies the referrer, and NULL means no referrer.
questions.rationale: Nullable anti-membership transfers to a known-country exclusion; lesson makes UNKNOWN explicit.
questions.solution: SELECT v.id FROM viewers v WHERE NOT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM viewers r WHERE r.referred_by=v.id)

questions.title: NOT IN and the NULL trap · Challenge 2
questions.prompt: Return id and country for viewers outside US and GB.
questions.rationale: Nullable anti-membership transfers to a known-country exclusion; lesson makes UNKNOWN explicit.
questions.solution: SELECT id,country FROM viewers WHERE country NOT IN('US','GB')

questions.title: Readable queries with CTEs · Challenge 1
questions.prompt: Use a CTE to return customer_id and units for store_customers whose total quantity exceeds 3.
questions.rationale: Two named aggregate CTEs reinforce decomposition before windows; no unnecessary staging tables.
questions.solution: WITH totals AS(SELECT customer_id,SUM(quantity) AS units FROM store_orders GROUP BY customer_id) SELECT customer_id,units FROM totals WHERE units>3

questions.title: Readable queries with CTEs · Challenge 2
questions.prompt: Use a CTE to return category and avg_price for categories with average price greater than 30.
questions.rationale: Two named aggregate CTEs reinforce decomposition before windows; no unnecessary staging tables.
questions.solution: WITH averages AS(SELECT category,AVG(price) AS avg_price FROM store_products GROUP BY category) SELECT category,avg_price FROM averages WHERE avg_price>30

questions.title: Dates & monthly analysis · Challenge 1
questions.prompt: Return month (YYYY-MM) and trip_count for every observed pickup month in trips.
questions.rationale: Mobility pickup-month trip counts transfer to card meter-fare totals; pickup time, cents and tips are distinguished.
questions.solution: SELECT substr(picked_up_at,1,7) AS month,COUNT(*) AS trip_count FROM trips GROUP BY month

questions.title: Dates & monthly analysis · Challenge 2
questions.prompt: Return month (YYYY-MM) and fare_cents for pickup months. Sum meter fare_cents only for card payments (payment_type=1); exclude tips.
questions.rationale: Mobility pickup-month trip counts transfer to card meter-fare totals; pickup time, cents and tips are distinguished.
questions.solution: SELECT substr(picked_up_at,1,7) AS month,SUM(fare_cents) AS fare_cents FROM trips WHERE payment_type=1 GROUP BY month

questions.title: Clean strings & cast values · Challenge 1
questions.prompt: Return id and clean_email for every member: trim outside spaces and lowercase the email; preserve NULL.
questions.rationale: Normalization transfers to domain extraction; preserving NULL is explicit, and this is not general email validation.
questions.solution: SELECT id,LOWER(TRIM(email)) AS clean_email FROM members

questions.title: Clean strings & cast values · Challenge 2
questions.prompt: Return id and email_domain: lowercase, trim, and take the email text after @. Preserve NULL.
questions.rationale: Normalization transfers to domain extraction; preserving NULL is explicit, and this is not general email validation.
questions.solution: SELECT id,SUBSTR(LOWER(TRIM(email)),INSTR(TRIM(email),'@')+1) AS email_domain FROM members

questions.title: Date boundaries & monthly buckets · Challenge 1
questions.difficultyWhy: Reviewed (rubric said warmup, score 0): Inclusive/exclusive month boundary reasoning is the point of the task.
questions.prompt: Return id and scheduled_departure for flights scheduled in January 2025, including the full final day and excluding February.
questions.rationale: Flight schedule boundaries use explicit UTC half-open intervals; transfer counts distinct scheduled aircraft by month.
questions.solution: SELECT id,scheduled_departure FROM flights WHERE scheduled_departure>='2025-01-01T00:00:00Z' AND scheduled_departure<'2025-02-01T00:00:00Z'

questions.title: Date boundaries & monthly buckets · Challenge 2
questions.prompt: Return month (YYYY-MM) and scheduled_aircraft: distinct aircraft_id values in each scheduled-departure month. Include cancelled flights.
questions.rationale: Flight schedule boundaries use explicit UTC half-open intervals; transfer counts distinct scheduled aircraft by month.
questions.solution: SELECT substr(scheduled_departure,1,7) AS month,COUNT(DISTINCT aircraft_id) AS scheduled_aircraft FROM flights GROUP BY month

questions.title: Window functions: ROW_NUMBER · Challenge 1
questions.prompt: Return id, customer_id and order_number: number each customer's store_orders by ordered_at then id.
questions.rationale: Chronological row numbering transfers to partitioned price ordering with deterministic ties.
questions.solution: SELECT id,customer_id,ROW_NUMBER() OVER(PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY ordered_at,id) AS order_number FROM store_orders

questions.title: Window functions: ROW_NUMBER · Challenge 2
questions.prompt: Return name, category and price_rank: number store_products within category by price descending then id.
questions.rationale: Chronological row numbering transfers to partitioned price ordering with deterministic ties.
questions.solution: SELECT name,category,ROW_NUMBER() OVER(PARTITION BY category ORDER BY price DESC,id) AS price_rank FROM store_products

questions.title: RANK & DENSE_RANK · Challenge 1
questions.prompt: Return player_id, goals and rank for every player. goals is the total across appearances, zero with none. Use RANK by goals descending; equal totals share a rank.
questions.rationale: Sports goal ranking includes unused players; transfer ranks within teams and distinguishes RANK from DENSE_RANK.
questions.solution: WITH totals AS (SELECT p.id AS player_id,COALESCE(SUM(a.goals),0) AS goals FROM players p LEFT JOIN appearances a ON a.player_id=p.id GROUP BY p.id) SELECT player_id,goals,RANK() OVER(ORDER BY goals DESC) AS rank FROM totals

questions.title: RANK & DENSE_RANK · Challenge 2
questions.prompt: Return player_id, team_id, goals and rank for every player. Rank total goals within the registered team using DENSE_RANK descending, with zero goals for players without appearances.
questions.rationale: Sports goal ranking includes unused players; transfer ranks within teams and distinguishes RANK from DENSE_RANK.
questions.solution: WITH totals AS (SELECT p.id AS player_id,p.team_id,COALESCE(SUM(a.goals),0) AS goals FROM players p LEFT JOIN appearances a ON a.player_id=p.id GROUP BY p.id) SELECT player_id,team_id,goals,DENSE_RANK() OVER(PARTITION BY team_id ORDER BY goals DESC) AS rank FROM totals

questions.title: Running totals · Challenge 1
questions.prompt: Return id, amount_cents and running_debits_cents for every settlement. Accumulate amount_cents by posted_at then id using a ROWS frame.
questions.rationale: Payments cumulative posted debits transfer from global to account partitions; explicitly excludes refunds and starting balance.
questions.solution: SELECT id,amount_cents,SUM(amount_cents) OVER(ORDER BY posted_at,id ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS running_debits_cents FROM settlements

questions.title: Running totals · Challenge 2
questions.prompt: Return settlement_id, account_id and running_debits_cents for every settlement. Accumulate only that account’s settlements, ordered by posted_at then settlement id.
questions.rationale: Payments cumulative posted debits transfer from global to account partitions; explicitly excludes refunds and starting balance.
questions.solution: SELECT s.id AS settlement_id,a.account_id,SUM(s.amount_cents) OVER(PARTITION BY a.account_id ORDER BY s.posted_at,s.id ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS running_debits_cents FROM settlements s JOIN authorizations a ON a.id=s.authorization_id

questions.title: Logical query processing & row grain · Challenge 1
questions.prompt: Return customer_id and units for paid store_orders grouped by customer; keep groups with units >2. Sort units descending, then customer_id ascending.
questions.rationale: Grouped totals contrast with a window retaining every input row; the quiz tests logical WHERE order.
questions.solution: SELECT customer_id,SUM(quantity) AS units FROM store_orders WHERE status='paid' GROUP BY customer_id HAVING SUM(quantity)>2 ORDER BY units DESC,customer_id

questions.title: Logical query processing & row grain · Challenge 2
questions.prompt: Keep every paid order row and return id, customer_id, quantity and customer_units (sum of paid quantity for that customer using a window).
questions.rationale: Grouped totals contrast with a window retaining every input row; the quiz tests logical WHERE order.
questions.solution: SELECT id,customer_id,quantity,SUM(quantity) OVER(PARTITION BY customer_id) AS customer_units FROM store_orders WHERE status='paid'

questions.title: Compare rows with LAG · Challenge 1
questions.prompt: Return id, route_id and previous_delay for every scheduled flight. previous_delay is the departure_delay_minutes of the previous scheduled flight on that route, ordered by scheduled_departure then id. Keep cancelled flights and their NULL delays.
questions.rationale: Flight predecessor selection transfers from all scheduled rows to operated rows before LAG; cancellations change membership.
questions.solution: SELECT id,route_id,LAG(departure_delay_minutes) OVER(PARTITION BY route_id ORDER BY scheduled_departure,id) AS previous_delay FROM flights

questions.title: Compare rows with LAG · Challenge 2
questions.prompt: Return id, route_id and delay_change for operated flights only (cancelled=0). Compare departure_delay_minutes with the previous operated flight on the same route, ordered by scheduled_departure then id. The first operated flight on each route has NULL change.
questions.rationale: Flight predecessor selection transfers from all scheduled rows to operated rows before LAG; cancellations change membership.
questions.solution: SELECT id,route_id,departure_delay_minutes-LAG(departure_delay_minutes) OVER(PARTITION BY route_id ORDER BY scheduled_departure,id) AS delay_change FROM flights WHERE cancelled=0

questions.title: Latest row per group · Challenge 1
questions.prompt: Return id, customer_id and ordered_at for the latest order per customer; break date ties by highest id.
questions.rationale: Latest-per-customer transfers to highest-per-category with a different tie rule.
questions.solution: WITH ranked AS(SELECT *,ROW_NUMBER() OVER(PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY ordered_at DESC,id DESC) AS rn FROM store_orders) SELECT id,customer_id,ordered_at FROM ranked WHERE rn=1

questions.title: Latest row per group · Challenge 2
questions.prompt: Return name, category and price for the most expensive product per category; break price ties by lowest id.
questions.rationale: Latest-per-customer transfers to highest-per-category with a different tie rule.
questions.solution: WITH ranked AS(SELECT *,ROW_NUMBER() OVER(PARTITION BY category ORDER BY price DESC,id) AS rn FROM store_products) SELECT name,category,price FROM ranked WHERE rn=1

questions.title: LEAD & the next event · Challenge 1
questions.prompt: Return id, package_id and next_scan_at for every tracking_events row. The next scan is within the package, ordered by occurred_at then id.
questions.rationale: Logistics LEAD uses physical time and an id tie-breaker; transfer calculates seconds and retains final NULLs and raw retries.
questions.solution: SELECT id,package_id,LEAD(occurred_at) OVER(PARTITION BY package_id ORDER BY occurred_at,id) AS next_scan_at FROM tracking_events

questions.title: LEAD & the next event · Challenge 2
questions.prompt: Return id and seconds_to_next for every received scan. Use the same package order and subtract current occurred_at from the next occurred_at in seconds. The last scan gets NULL.
questions.rationale: Logistics LEAD uses physical time and an id tie-breaker; transfer calculates seconds and retains final NULLs and raw retries.
questions.solution: SELECT id,unixepoch(LEAD(occurred_at) OVER(PARTITION BY package_id ORDER BY occurred_at,id))-unixepoch(occurred_at) AS seconds_to_next FROM tracking_events

questions.title: FIRST_VALUE, LAST_VALUE & frames · Challenge 1
questions.prompt: Return device_id, observed_at and final_temperature_c for every sensor_readings row. Repeat that device’s final observed temperature across all its rows.
questions.rationale: IoT full-frame LAST_VALUE transfers to deviation from FIRST_VALUE; default frame and baseline semantics differ.
questions.solution: SELECT device_id,observed_at,LAST_VALUE(temperature_c) OVER(PARTITION BY device_id ORDER BY observed_at ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND UNBOUNDED FOLLOWING) AS final_temperature_c FROM sensor_readings

questions.title: FIRST_VALUE, LAST_VALUE & frames · Challenge 2
questions.prompt: Return device_id, observed_at and change_from_first_c: temperature_c minus the device’s first observed temperature, rounded to two decimals.
questions.rationale: IoT full-frame LAST_VALUE transfers to deviation from FIRST_VALUE; default frame and baseline semantics differ.
questions.solution: SELECT device_id,observed_at,ROUND(temperature_c-FIRST_VALUE(temperature_c) OVER(PARTITION BY device_id ORDER BY observed_at),2) AS change_from_first_c FROM sensor_readings

questions.title: Rolling averages & missing dates · Challenge 1
questions.prompt: Return station_id, date and rolling_tmax_c for usable TMAX observations only. Average current and previous two observed temperatures, divide raw tenths by 10.0 and round to two decimals. Usable means raw_value non-NULL and quality_flag NULL. Order by station_id,date.
questions.rationale: Weather observed-row averaging transfers to a complete calendar; absent temperatures stay unknown rather than invented zeros.
questions.solution: SELECT station_id,date,ROUND(AVG(raw_value/10.0) OVER(PARTITION BY station_id ORDER BY date ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW),2) AS rolling_tmax_c FROM daily_weather WHERE element='TMAX' AND raw_value IS NOT NULL AND quality_flag IS NULL ORDER BY station_id,date

questions.title: Rolling averages & missing dates · Challenge 2
questions.prompt: Return station_id, date and rolling_tmax_c for every station and calendar date. Average usable TMAX values in the current and previous two calendar dates, ignoring missing values; an entirely missing window is NULL. Round Celsius averages to two decimals. Order by station_id,date.
questions.rationale: Weather observed-row averaging transfers to a complete calendar; absent temperatures stay unknown rather than invented zeros.
questions.solution: SELECT s.id AS station_id,c.date,ROUND(AVG(w.raw_value/10.0) OVER(PARTITION BY s.id ORDER BY c.date ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW),2) AS rolling_tmax_c FROM stations s CROSS JOIN calendar c LEFT JOIN daily_weather w ON w.station_id=s.id AND w.date=c.date AND w.element='TMAX' AND w.quality_flag IS NULL ORDER BY s.id,c.date

questions.title: Share of total with windows · Challenge 1
questions.prompt: Return fuel, output_mw and share_pct of all generation. Sum output_mw by fuel; share_pct is 0–100, rounded to two decimals, or NULL if the denominator is zero.
questions.rationale: Energy global fuel share transfers to regional denominators; ratio of sums and zero-denominator handling are explicit.
questions.solution: SELECT fuel,SUM(output_mw) AS output_mw,ROUND(100.0*SUM(output_mw)/NULLIF(SUM(SUM(output_mw)) OVER(),0),2) AS share_pct FROM generation GROUP BY fuel

questions.title: Share of total with windows · Challenge 2
questions.prompt: Return region_id, fuel, output_mw and share_pct of that region’s generation, rounded to two decimals. Use NULL if a region’s total is zero.
questions.rationale: Energy global fuel share transfers to regional denominators; ratio of sums and zero-denominator handling are explicit.
questions.solution: SELECT region_id,fuel,SUM(output_mw) AS output_mw,ROUND(100.0*SUM(output_mw)/NULLIF(SUM(SUM(output_mw)) OVER(PARTITION BY region_id),0),2) AS share_pct FROM generation GROUP BY region_id,fuel

questions.title: Top N per group & ties · Challenge 1
questions.difficultyWhy: Reviewed (rubric said hard, score 9.5): Aggregate-then-rank top-N with an explicit tie-breaker; a standard intermediate pattern.
questions.prompt: Return creator_id, video_id and watch_seconds for the top 2 watched videos per creator, excluding videos with no events. Rank by total seconds descending, break ties by smallest video_id.
questions.rationale: Exactly two items transfers to all top ties; ROW_NUMBER and DENSE_RANK answer different business contracts.
questions.solution: WITH totals AS(SELECT v.creator_id,v.id AS video_id,SUM(w.watch_seconds) AS watch_seconds FROM videos v JOIN watch_events w ON w.video_id=v.id GROUP BY v.id,v.creator_id),ranked AS(SELECT *,ROW_NUMBER() OVER(PARTITION BY creator_id ORDER BY watch_seconds DESC,video_id) AS rn FROM totals) SELECT creator_id,video_id,watch_seconds FROM ranked WHERE rn<=2

questions.title: Top N per group & ties · Challenge 2
questions.difficultyWhy: Reviewed (rubric said hard, score 9.5): Top-N with ties via DENSE_RANK; the prompt states the tie rule.
questions.prompt: Return creator_id, video_id and watch_seconds for each creator's most-watched video(s), including ties. Exclude videos with no events.
questions.rationale: Exactly two items transfers to all top ties; ROW_NUMBER and DENSE_RANK answer different business contracts.
questions.solution: WITH totals AS(SELECT v.creator_id,v.id AS video_id,SUM(w.watch_seconds) AS watch_seconds FROM videos v JOIN watch_events w ON w.video_id=v.id GROUP BY v.id,v.creator_id),ranked AS(SELECT *,DENSE_RANK() OVER(PARTITION BY creator_id ORDER BY watch_seconds DESC) AS rn FROM totals) SELECT creator_id,video_id,watch_seconds FROM ranked WHERE rn=1

questions.title: NTILE & balanced ranking buckets · Challenge 1
questions.prompt: Return game_id, player_id, minutes and bucket using NTILE(4) across appearances, ordered in the window by minutes descending, game_id then player_id.
questions.rationale: Sports appearance buckets transfer from league-wide to team partitions; NTILE can split equal minutes.
questions.solution: SELECT game_id,player_id,minutes,NTILE(4) OVER(ORDER BY minutes DESC,game_id,player_id) AS bucket FROM appearances

questions.title: NTILE & balanced ranking buckets · Challenge 2
questions.prompt: Return game_id, player_id, team_id and bucket using NTILE(2) within each player’s registered team. Order by minutes descending, game_id then player_id.
questions.rationale: Sports appearance buckets transfer from league-wide to team partitions; NTILE can split equal minutes.
questions.solution: SELECT a.game_id,a.player_id,p.team_id,NTILE(2) OVER(PARTITION BY p.team_id ORDER BY a.minutes DESC,a.game_id,a.player_id) AS bucket FROM appearances a JOIN players p ON p.id=a.player_id

questions.title: Recursive CTEs · Challenge 1
questions.prompt: Use a recursive CTE to return n with integers 1 through 5.
questions.rationale: Recursive numeric anchor transfers to a multi-level developer hierarchy; acyclic input is a declared assumption.
questions.solution: WITH RECURSIVE numbers(n) AS(SELECT 1 UNION ALL SELECT n+1 FROM numbers WHERE n<5) SELECT n FROM numbers

questions.title: Recursive CTEs · Challenge 2
questions.prompt: Return developer_id and depth for every developer reachable from a root whose manager_id is NULL. Roots have depth 0; each reporting edge adds 1. The supplied management graph is acyclic. Use a recursive CTE to follow all levels.
questions.rationale: Recursive numeric anchor transfers to a multi-level developer hierarchy; acyclic input is a declared assumption.
questions.solution: WITH RECURSIVE tree(developer_id,depth) AS (SELECT id,0 FROM developers WHERE manager_id IS NULL UNION ALL SELECT d.id,t.depth+1 FROM developers d JOIN tree t ON d.manager_id=t.developer_id) SELECT developer_id,depth FROM tree

questions.title: Query plans & indexes · Challenge 1
questions.prompt: Show name for Chicago store_customers. Run the reference with Explain mode to inspect the plan.
questions.rationale: Keeps SQLite plan inspection conceptual; these two tasks stay lesson-only because they require Explain mode.
questions.solution: SELECT name FROM store_customers WHERE city='Chicago'

questions.title: Query plans & indexes · Challenge 2
questions.prompt: Show id and quantity for paid store_orders. Inspect its plan with Explain mode.
questions.rationale: Keeps SQLite plan inspection conceptual; these two tasks stay lesson-only because they require Explain mode.
questions.solution: SELECT id,quantity FROM store_orders WHERE status='paid'

questions.title: Capstone: customer insights · Challenge 1
questions.prompt: Show name, paid_revenue and revenue_rank for store_customers with paid store_orders. Use DENSE_RANK, highest revenue first in the rank calculation.
questions.rationale: Capstone combines joins, aggregates and dense ranking at two reporting grains; repetition is deliberate synthesis.
questions.solution: WITH revenue AS(SELECT c.name,SUM(o.quantity*p.price) AS paid_revenue FROM store_customers c JOIN store_orders o ON o.customer_id=c.id JOIN store_products p ON p.id=o.product_id WHERE o.status='paid' GROUP BY c.id,c.name) SELECT name,paid_revenue,DENSE_RANK() OVER(ORDER BY paid_revenue DESC) AS revenue_rank FROM revenue

questions.title: Capstone: customer insights · Challenge 2
questions.prompt: Show category, paid_revenue and revenue_rank for product categories with paid store_orders. Use DENSE_RANK by revenue descending.
questions.rationale: Capstone combines joins, aggregates and dense ranking at two reporting grains; repetition is deliberate synthesis.
questions.solution: WITH revenue AS(SELECT p.category,SUM(o.quantity*p.price) AS paid_revenue FROM store_orders o JOIN store_products p ON p.id=o.product_id WHERE o.status='paid' GROUP BY p.category) SELECT category,paid_revenue,DENSE_RANK() OVER(ORDER BY paid_revenue DESC) AS revenue_rank FROM revenue

questions.title: Deduplicate event retries · Challenge 1
questions.prompt: Return id, event_key and member_id for the latest ingested row of each event_key. Break ingestion ties by highest id.
questions.rationale: Latest ingestion per event key transfers to summaries after deduplication; id resolves ingestion-time ties.
questions.solution: WITH ranked AS(SELECT *,ROW_NUMBER() OVER(PARTITION BY event_key ORDER BY ingested_at DESC,id DESC) AS rn FROM social_events) SELECT id,event_key,member_id FROM ranked WHERE rn=1

questions.title: Deduplicate event retries · Challenge 2
questions.prompt: After keeping the latest ingested row per event_key (tie: highest id), return event_type and event_count by event_type.
questions.rationale: Latest ingestion per event key transfers to summaries after deduplication; id resolves ingestion-time ties.
questions.solution: WITH ranked AS(SELECT *,ROW_NUMBER() OVER(PARTITION BY event_key ORDER BY ingested_at DESC,id DESC) AS rn FROM social_events) SELECT event_type,COUNT(*) AS event_count FROM ranked WHERE rn=1 GROUP BY event_type

questions.title: Daily active users & engagement · Challenge 1
questions.prompt: Return day (YYYY-MM-DD) and active_viewers (distinct viewers) for every observed watch date.
questions.rationale: Distinct daily audience transfers to minutes per active viewer; numerator and denominator share the same day population.
questions.solution: SELECT date(watched_at) AS day,COUNT(DISTINCT viewer_id) AS active_viewers FROM watch_events GROUP BY day

questions.title: Daily active users & engagement · Challenge 2
questions.prompt: Return day, active_viewers and minutes_per_active_viewer, rounded to 2 decimals, for each observed watch date.
questions.rationale: Distinct daily audience transfers to minutes per active viewer; numerator and denominator share the same day population.
questions.solution: SELECT date(watched_at) AS day,COUNT(DISTINCT viewer_id) AS active_viewers,ROUND(SUM(watch_seconds)/60.0/COUNT(DISTINCT viewer_id),2) AS minutes_per_active_viewer FROM watch_events GROUP BY day

questions.title: Ordered conversion funnels · Challenge 1
questions.prompt: Return one row: viewed, signed_up, purchased as member counts for the ordered view → signup → purchase funnel. Equal times are allowed; use each member's earliest valid next step.
questions.rationale: Ordered funnel counts transfer to member-level evidence; earliest valid next steps prevent unordered event membership shortcuts.
questions.solution: WITH views AS(SELECT member_id,MIN(event_at) AS viewed_at FROM social_events WHERE event_type='view' GROUP BY member_id), signups AS(SELECT v.member_id,v.viewed_at,MIN(e.event_at) AS signed_at FROM views v LEFT JOIN social_events e ON e.member_id=v.member_id AND e.event_type='signup' AND e.event_at>=v.viewed_at GROUP BY v.member_id,v.viewed_at), funnel AS(SELECT s.member_id,s.viewed_at,s.signed_at,MIN(e.event_at) AS purchased_at FROM signups s LEFT JOIN social_events e ON e.member_id=s.member_id AND e.event_type='purchase' AND e.event_at>=s.signed_at GROUP BY s.member_id,s.viewed_at,s.signed_at) SELECT COUNT(*) AS viewed,COUNT(signed_at) AS signed_up,COUNT(purchased_at) AS purchased FROM funnel

questions.title: Ordered conversion funnels · Challenge 2
questions.prompt: Return member_id, viewed_at, signed_at and purchased_at for members who complete that ordered funnel.
questions.rationale: Ordered funnel counts transfer to member-level evidence; earliest valid next steps prevent unordered event membership shortcuts.
questions.solution: WITH views AS(SELECT member_id,MIN(event_at) AS viewed_at FROM social_events WHERE event_type='view' GROUP BY member_id), signups AS(SELECT v.member_id,v.viewed_at,MIN(e.event_at) AS signed_at FROM views v LEFT JOIN social_events e ON e.member_id=v.member_id AND e.event_type='signup' AND e.event_at>=v.viewed_at GROUP BY v.member_id,v.viewed_at), funnel AS(SELECT s.member_id,s.viewed_at,s.signed_at,MIN(e.event_at) AS purchased_at FROM signups s LEFT JOIN social_events e ON e.member_id=s.member_id AND e.event_type='purchase' AND e.event_at>=s.signed_at GROUP BY s.member_id,s.viewed_at,s.signed_at) SELECT member_id,viewed_at,signed_at,purchased_at FROM funnel WHERE purchased_at IS NOT NULL

questions.title: Cohorts & exact-day retention · Challenge 1
questions.prompt: With observation cutoff Jan 15 2025, return cohort_day, cohort_size, retained_viewers and retention_pct (0–100, 2 decimals) for exact-day D1 retention. Include only mature cohorts.
questions.rationale: D1 and D7 are intentional repetition because cohort maturity changes at the fixed observation cutoff; second stays lesson-only.
questions.solution: SELECT v.signup_at AS cohort_day,COUNT(*) AS cohort_size,SUM(CASE WHEN EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM watch_events w WHERE w.viewer_id=v.id AND date(w.watched_at)=date(v.signup_at,'+1 days')) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS retained_viewers,ROUND(100.0*SUM(CASE WHEN EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM watch_events w WHERE w.viewer_id=v.id AND date(w.watched_at)=date(v.signup_at,'+1 days')) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)/COUNT(*),2) AS retention_pct FROM viewers v WHERE v.signup_at<=date('2025-01-15','-1 days') GROUP BY v.signup_at

questions.title: Cohorts & exact-day retention · Challenge 2
questions.prompt: Use the same output and cutoff for exact-day D7 retention (signup date +7 days); include only mature cohorts.
questions.rationale: D1 and D7 are intentional repetition because cohort maturity changes at the fixed observation cutoff; second stays lesson-only.
questions.solution: SELECT v.signup_at AS cohort_day,COUNT(*) AS cohort_size,SUM(CASE WHEN EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM watch_events w WHERE w.viewer_id=v.id AND date(w.watched_at)=date(v.signup_at,'+7 days')) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS retained_viewers,ROUND(100.0*SUM(CASE WHEN EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM watch_events w WHERE w.viewer_id=v.id AND date(w.watched_at)=date(v.signup_at,'+7 days')) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)/COUNT(*),2) AS retention_pct FROM viewers v WHERE v.signup_at<=date('2025-01-15','-7 days') GROUP BY v.signup_at

questions.title: Sessionize an event stream · Challenge 1
questions.prompt: Using raw social_events, return member_id and session_count. Start a new session on the first event or a gap of at least 30 minutes; order by event_at then id per member.
questions.rationale: Session counts transfer to row-level labels; first row and exact 30-minute boundaries are stated, second stays lesson-only.
questions.solution: WITH previous AS(SELECT *,LAG(event_at) OVER(PARTITION BY member_id ORDER BY event_at,id) AS previous_at FROM social_events), marked AS(SELECT *,CASE WHEN previous_at IS NULL OR unixepoch(event_at)-unixepoch(previous_at)>=1800 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS new_session FROM previous), numbered AS(SELECT *,SUM(new_session) OVER(PARTITION BY member_id ORDER BY event_at,id ROWS UNBOUNDED PRECEDING) AS session_number FROM marked) SELECT member_id,MAX(session_number) AS session_count FROM numbered GROUP BY member_id

questions.title: Sessionize an event stream · Challenge 2
questions.prompt: Using the same rule, return id, member_id and session_number for every raw social event.
questions.rationale: Session counts transfer to row-level labels; first row and exact 30-minute boundaries are stated, second stays lesson-only.
questions.solution: WITH previous AS(SELECT *,LAG(event_at) OVER(PARTITION BY member_id ORDER BY event_at,id) AS previous_at FROM social_events), marked AS(SELECT *,CASE WHEN previous_at IS NULL OR unixepoch(event_at)-unixepoch(previous_at)>=1800 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS new_session FROM previous), numbered AS(SELECT *,SUM(new_session) OVER(PARTITION BY member_id ORDER BY event_at,id ROWS UNBOUNDED PRECEDING) AS session_number FROM marked) SELECT id,member_id,session_number FROM numbered

questions.title: Multi-grain joins without fan-out · Challenge 1
questions.prompt: Return id, request_count and billed_amount for every account across all dates. Aggregate requests and invoices separately to avoid multiplication; use zeros for missing totals.
questions.rationale: Request count transfers to successful tokens while independently aggregated invoices preserve account grain.
questions.solution: WITH usage AS(SELECT account_id,COUNT(*) AS request_count FROM ai_requests GROUP BY account_id),billing AS(SELECT account_id,SUM(billed_amount) AS billed_amount FROM invoices GROUP BY account_id) SELECT a.id,COALESCE(u.request_count,0) AS request_count,COALESCE(b.billed_amount,0) AS billed_amount FROM ai_accounts a LEFT JOIN usage u ON u.account_id=a.id LEFT JOIN billing b ON b.account_id=a.id

questions.title: Multi-grain joins without fan-out · Challenge 2
questions.prompt: Return id, output_tokens and billed_amount for every account across all dates. Sum only successful output tokens and aggregate invoices separately. Use zeros for missing totals.
questions.rationale: Request count transfers to successful tokens while independently aggregated invoices preserve account grain.
questions.solution: WITH usage AS(SELECT account_id,SUM(output_tokens) AS output_tokens FROM ai_requests WHERE status='success' GROUP BY account_id),billing AS(SELECT account_id,SUM(billed_amount) AS billed_amount FROM invoices GROUP BY account_id) SELECT a.id,COALESCE(u.output_tokens,0) AS output_tokens,COALESCE(b.billed_amount,0) AS billed_amount FROM ai_accounts a LEFT JOIN usage u ON u.account_id=a.id LEFT JOIN billing b ON b.account_id=a.id

questions.title: Revenue & payment reconciliation · Challenge 1
questions.prompt: Return id, billed_amount, net_collected and gap for every invoice across all periods. Net collected = invoice_payments - invoice_refunds; gap = billed - net collected. Treat missing totals as zero.
questions.rationale: Invoice reconciliation transfers to exceptions-only output; shared definition is retained and second stays lesson-only.
questions.solution: WITH paid AS(SELECT invoice_id,SUM(amount) AS paid_amount FROM invoice_payments GROUP BY invoice_id),returned AS(SELECT invoice_id,SUM(amount) AS refund_amount FROM invoice_refunds GROUP BY invoice_id) SELECT i.id,i.billed_amount,COALESCE(p.paid_amount,0)-COALESCE(r.refund_amount,0) AS net_collected,i.billed_amount-COALESCE(p.paid_amount,0)+COALESCE(r.refund_amount,0) AS gap FROM invoices i LEFT JOIN paid p ON p.invoice_id=i.id LEFT JOIN returned r ON r.invoice_id=i.id

questions.title: Revenue & payment reconciliation · Challenge 2
questions.prompt: Using the same definition, return invoice_id and gap only for invoices with nonzero gap.
questions.rationale: Invoice reconciliation transfers to exceptions-only output; shared definition is retained and second stays lesson-only.
questions.solution: WITH paid AS(SELECT invoice_id,SUM(amount) AS paid_amount FROM invoice_payments GROUP BY invoice_id),returned AS(SELECT invoice_id,SUM(amount) AS refund_amount FROM invoice_refunds GROUP BY invoice_id), result AS(SELECT i.id AS invoice_id,i.billed_amount-COALESCE(p.paid_amount,0)+COALESCE(r.refund_amount,0) AS gap FROM invoices i LEFT JOIN paid p ON p.invoice_id=i.id LEFT JOIN returned r ON r.invoice_id=i.id) SELECT invoice_id,gap FROM result WHERE gap<>0

questions.title: AI usage cost & contribution margin · Challenge 1
questions.prompt: Return model and usage_cost in fictional USD, rounded to 6 decimals, for successful requests across all dates.
questions.rationale: Model costs transfer to account contribution margin in a fixed month; fictional prices and non-profit limitation are explicit.
questions.solution: SELECT r.model,ROUND(SUM(r.input_tokens*m.input_per_million+r.output_tokens*m.output_per_million)/1000000.0,6) AS usage_cost FROM ai_requests r JOIN model_rates m ON m.model=r.model WHERE r.status='success' GROUP BY r.model

questions.title: AI usage cost & contribution margin · Challenge 2
questions.prompt: Return id, billed_amount, usage_cost and contribution_margin for every account for Jan 2025. Use January invoices and successful requests only; missing totals are zero. Round cost and margin to 6 decimals. Margin = billed - usage cost.
questions.rationale: Model costs transfer to account contribution margin in a fixed month; fictional prices and non-profit limitation are explicit.
questions.solution: WITH costs AS(SELECT r.account_id,SUM(r.input_tokens*m.input_per_million+r.output_tokens*m.output_per_million)/1000000.0 AS usage_cost FROM ai_requests r JOIN model_rates m ON m.model=r.model WHERE r.status='success' AND r.requested_at>='2025-01-01' AND r.requested_at<'2025-02-01' GROUP BY r.account_id),billing AS(SELECT account_id,SUM(billed_amount) AS billed_amount FROM invoices WHERE period='2025-01' GROUP BY account_id) SELECT a.id,COALESCE(b.billed_amount,0) AS billed_amount,ROUND(COALESCE(c.usage_cost,0),6) AS usage_cost,ROUND(COALESCE(b.billed_amount,0)-COALESCE(c.usage_cost,0),6) AS contribution_margin FROM ai_accounts a LEFT JOIN costs c ON c.account_id=a.id LEFT JOIN billing b ON b.account_id=a.id

questions.title: Experiment conversion denominators · Challenge 1
questions.prompt: Return variant, assigned, converted and conversion_pct (0–100, 2 decimals). A member converts with any purchase on/after assigned_at and before Feb 1 2025. Include all assigned members.
questions.rationale: Assigned-user conversion rates transfer to per-assignment flags; the same post-assignment rule preserves the denominator.
questions.solution: WITH results AS(SELECT a.member_id,a.variant,CASE WHEN EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM social_events e WHERE e.member_id=a.member_id AND e.event_type='purchase' AND e.event_at>=a.assigned_at AND e.event_at<'2025-02-01') THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS converted FROM experiment_assignments a) SELECT variant,COUNT(*) AS assigned,SUM(converted) AS converted,ROUND(100.0*SUM(converted)/COUNT(*),2) AS conversion_pct FROM results GROUP BY variant

questions.title: Experiment conversion denominators · Challenge 2
questions.prompt: Return member_id, variant and converted (1 or 0) for every assignment using the same post-assignment purchase definition and cutoff.
questions.rationale: Assigned-user conversion rates transfer to per-assignment flags; the same post-assignment rule preserves the denominator.
questions.solution: SELECT a.member_id,a.variant,CASE WHEN EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM social_events e WHERE e.member_id=a.member_id AND e.event_type='purchase' AND e.event_at>=a.assigned_at AND e.event_at<'2025-02-01') THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS converted FROM experiment_assignments a

questions.prompt: Begin a transaction, add 10 to every lab item price, then roll back. Return id and price; all values should be original.

questions.title: Views: reusable query definitions · Challenge 1
questions.prompt: Create view paid_orders exposing id, customer_id and quantity for paid store_orders. Return those columns by selecting the view.

questions.title: Views: reusable query definitions · Challenge 2

questions.title: CTEs, CTAS & temporary tables · Challenge 1
questions.prompt: Materialize a TEMP table customer_units with customer_id and total quantity as units. Return customer_id and units for units >3.

questions.title: CTEs, CTAS & temporary tables · Challenge 2

questions.title: Triggers & visible audit effects · Challenge 1
questions.difficultyWhy: Reviewed (rubric said medium, score 5): Trigger syntax is new but the logic is a single audit insert.
questions.prompt: Create a price_audit trigger AFTER UPDATE OF price on inventory_items, logging changed prices in inventory_audit; add 5 to id=1 price. Return item_id,old_price,new_price from inventory_audit.
questions.rationale: Single-row trigger exercise transfers to multi-row updates and audit effects; second needs the first trigger definition.
questions.solution: CREATE TRIGGER price_audit AFTER UPDATE OF price ON inventory_items WHEN OLD.price<>NEW.price BEGIN INSERT INTO inventory_audit VALUES(NEW.id,OLD.price,NEW.price); END; UPDATE inventory_items SET price=price+5 WHERE id=1; SELECT item_id,old_price,new_price FROM inventory_audit

questions.title: Triggers & visible audit effects · Challenge 2
questions.difficultyWhy: Reviewed (rubric said medium, score 5): Same trigger plus one UPDATE.
questions.prompt: Create the same trigger, then double prices for all items with price<50. Return item_id,old_price,new_price from inventory_audit.
questions.rationale: Single-row trigger exercise transfers to multi-row updates and audit effects; second needs the first trigger definition.
questions.solution: CREATE TRIGGER price_audit AFTER UPDATE OF price ON inventory_items WHEN OLD.price<>NEW.price BEGIN INSERT INTO inventory_audit VALUES(NEW.id,OLD.price,NEW.price); END; UPDATE inventory_items SET price=price*2 WHERE price<50; SELECT item_id,old_price,new_price FROM inventory_audit

questions.prompt: Create idx_orders_customer on store_orders(customer_id), then return id and quantity for customer_id=1. Run Query plan after the script to inspect the final SELECT.

questions.title: SARGable ranges, not speed commandments · Challenge 1

questions.title: Review AI-generated SQL with evidence · Challenge 1
questions.prompt: Fix the proposed COUNT(*) LEFT JOIN query. Return id and request_count for every account, including zero-request accounts.

questions.title: Review AI-generated SQL with evidence · Challenge 2
questions.difficultyWhy: Reviewed (rubric said hard, score 6): Fixing integer division and a filter in a given query; guided by the prompt.
questions.prompt: Fix an AI query that divides integers or filters out inactive accounts. Return id and success_pct for every account, NULL with no requests, 2 decimals.

questions.solution: SELECT a.id,ROUND(100.0*SUM(CASE WHEN r.status='success' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)/NULLIF(COUNT(r.id),0),2) AS success_pct FROM ai_accounts a LEFT JOIN ai_requests r ON r.account_id=a.id GROUP BY a.id

questions.title: Bronze: inspect raw data before cleaning · Challenge 1
questions.prompt: Return customer_id (trimmed raw_id) and versions for non-NULL duplicate customer keys in bronze_customers. Keep only keys with more than one version.

questions.solution: SELECT TRIM(raw_id) AS customer_id,COUNT(*) AS versions FROM bronze_customers WHERE raw_id IS NOT NULL GROUP BY TRIM(raw_id) HAVING COUNT(*)>1

questions.title: Bronze: inspect raw data before cleaning · Challenge 2
questions.difficultyWhy: Reviewed (rubric said warmup, score 0.5): Invalid-date detection via date() returning NULL is a non-obvious idea.
questions.prompt: Return row_id and order_date for bronze sales whose date is invalid (date(order_date) IS NULL).
questions.rationale: Duplicate-key profiling transfers to invalid-date profiling without changing raw evidence.
questions.solution: SELECT row_id,order_date FROM bronze_sales WHERE date(order_date) IS NULL

questions.title: Silver: clean, map & deduplicate · Challenge 1
questions.prompt: Create TEMP silver_customers: trim keys/names; discard NULL/empty keys; keep latest updated_at per trimmed key. Map US/USA→United States, GB/UK→United Kingdom, IND→India, CA→Canada. Return customer_id,name,country.
questions.rationale: Builds cleaned latest customer rows, then summarizes mapped countries; second retains its prerequisite TEMP-table contract.
questions.solution: CREATE TEMP TABLE silver_customers AS WITH ranked AS(SELECT *,ROW_NUMBER() OVER(PARTITION BY TRIM(raw_id) ORDER BY updated_at DESC) AS rn FROM bronze_customers WHERE raw_id IS NOT NULL AND TRIM(raw_id)<>'') SELECT TRIM(raw_id) AS customer_id,TRIM(name) AS name,CASE UPPER(TRIM(country)) WHEN 'US' THEN 'United States' WHEN 'USA' THEN 'United States' WHEN 'UK' THEN 'United Kingdom' WHEN 'GB' THEN 'United Kingdom' WHEN 'IND' THEN 'India' WHEN 'CA' THEN 'Canada' ELSE UPPER(TRIM(country)) END AS country FROM ranked WHERE rn=1; SELECT customer_id,name,country FROM silver_customers

questions.title: Silver: clean, map & deduplicate · Challenge 2
questions.prompt: Create the same TEMP silver_customers, then return country and customer_count per mapped country.
questions.rationale: Builds cleaned latest customer rows, then summarizes mapped countries; second retains its prerequisite TEMP-table contract.
questions.solution: CREATE TEMP TABLE silver_customers AS WITH ranked AS(SELECT *,ROW_NUMBER() OVER(PARTITION BY TRIM(raw_id) ORDER BY updated_at DESC) AS rn FROM bronze_customers WHERE raw_id IS NOT NULL AND TRIM(raw_id)<>'') SELECT TRIM(raw_id) AS customer_id,TRIM(name) AS name,CASE UPPER(TRIM(country)) WHEN 'US' THEN 'United States' WHEN 'USA' THEN 'United States' WHEN 'UK' THEN 'United Kingdom' WHEN 'GB' THEN 'United Kingdom' WHEN 'IND' THEN 'India' WHEN 'CA' THEN 'Canada' ELSE UPPER(TRIM(country)) END AS country FROM ranked WHERE rn=1; SELECT country,COUNT(*) AS customer_count FROM silver_customers GROUP BY country

questions.title: Gold: dimensions, facts & quality gates · Challenge 1
questions.prompt: Build TEMP built_fact from bronze_sales and dimension lookups. Validate numeric positive quantity, valid date and matching trimmed natural keys. Recompute sales = quantity × dim_product.price. Return sale_key,customer_key,product_key,quantity,sales,order_date.
questions.rationale: Accepted fact construction transfers to reconciliation of rejected rows; state validation checks the built table.
questions.solution: CREATE TEMP TABLE built_fact AS SELECT b.row_id AS sale_key,c.customer_key,p.product_key,CAST(b.quantity AS INTEGER) AS quantity,CAST(b.quantity AS INTEGER)*p.price AS sales,b.order_date FROM bronze_sales b JOIN dim_customer c ON c.customer_id=TRIM(b.customer_id) JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_id=TRIM(b.product_id) WHERE TRIM(b.quantity)<>'' AND TRIM(b.quantity) NOT GLOB '*[^0-9]*' AND CAST(b.quantity AS INTEGER)>0 AND b.order_date GLOB '[0-9][0-9][0-9][0-9]-[0-9][0-9]-[0-9][0-9]' AND date(b.order_date,'+0 days')=b.order_date; SELECT sale_key,customer_key,product_key,quantity,sales,order_date FROM built_fact

questions.title: Gold: dimensions, facts & quality gates · Challenge 2
questions.prompt: Build the same TEMP built_fact; return rejected_rows as source row count minus built fact row count.
questions.rationale: Accepted fact construction transfers to reconciliation of rejected rows; state validation checks the built table.
questions.solution: CREATE TEMP TABLE built_fact AS SELECT b.row_id AS sale_key,c.customer_key,p.product_key,CAST(b.quantity AS INTEGER) AS quantity,CAST(b.quantity AS INTEGER)*p.price AS sales,b.order_date FROM bronze_sales b JOIN dim_customer c ON c.customer_id=TRIM(b.customer_id) JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_id=TRIM(b.product_id) WHERE TRIM(b.quantity)<>'' AND TRIM(b.quantity) NOT GLOB '*[^0-9]*' AND CAST(b.quantity AS INTEGER)>0 AND b.order_date GLOB '[0-9][0-9][0-9][0-9]-[0-9][0-9]-[0-9][0-9]' AND date(b.order_date,'+0 days')=b.order_date; SELECT (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM bronze_sales)-(SELECT COUNT(*) FROM built_fact) AS rejected_rows

questions.title: EDA: explore before telling the story · Challenge 1
questions.prompt: Return first_sale, last_sale, sales_lines and total_sales as one summary row from fact_sales.
questions.rationale: Basic extent/count/total profiling transfers to a metric-union report; literal output labels remain part of the contract.
questions.solution: SELECT MIN(order_date) AS first_sale,MAX(order_date) AS last_sale,COUNT(*) AS sales_lines,SUM(sales) AS total_sales FROM fact_sales

questions.title: EDA: explore before telling the story · Challenge 2
questions.prompt: Return metric and value using UNION ALL for Total sales (sum of sales), Units (sum of quantity), and Active customers (distinct customer_key) from fact_sales.
questions.rationale: Basic extent/count/total profiling transfers to a metric-union report; literal output labels remain part of the contract.
questions.solution: SELECT 'Total sales' AS metric,SUM(sales) AS value FROM fact_sales UNION ALL SELECT 'Units',SUM(quantity) FROM fact_sales UNION ALL SELECT 'Active customers',COUNT(DISTINCT customer_key) FROM fact_sales

questions.title: Customer & product reporting contracts · Challenge 1
questions.prompt: Return customer_id,name,sales_lines,total_sales,recency_days for every dim_customer. Missing sales total=0; recency=NULL with no sales. Recency = days from last order_date to 2025-04-01, integer.
questions.rationale: Customer recency transfers to product segmentation while preserving inactive dimensions; zero totals differ from NULL recency.
questions.solution: SELECT c.customer_id,c.name,COUNT(f.sale_key) AS sales_lines,COALESCE(SUM(f.sales),0) AS total_sales,CAST(julianday('2025-04-01')-julianday(MAX(f.order_date)) AS INTEGER) AS recency_days FROM dim_customer c LEFT JOIN fact_sales f ON f.customer_key=c.customer_key GROUP BY c.customer_key,c.customer_id,c.name

questions.title: Customer & product reporting contracts · Challenge 2
questions.prompt: Return product_id,name,total_sales,total_units,performance_segment for every dim_product. Missing totals=0. High if total_sales>=200, otherwise Standard.
questions.rationale: Customer recency transfers to product segmentation while preserving inactive dimensions; zero totals differ from NULL recency.
questions.solution: SELECT p.product_id,p.name,COALESCE(SUM(f.sales),0) AS total_sales,COALESCE(SUM(f.quantity),0) AS total_units,CASE WHEN COALESCE(SUM(f.sales),0)>=200 THEN 'High' ELSE 'Standard' END AS performance_segment FROM dim_product p LEFT JOIN fact_sales f ON f.product_key=p.product_key GROUP BY p.product_key,p.product_id,p.name

questions.title: Monthly change & cumulative reports · Challenge 1
questions.prompt: Return month (YYYY-MM),sales,running_sales for observed months; cumulative sales ordered by month. Sort output by month.
questions.rationale: Monthly cumulative sales transfer to percentage change; comparison is previous observed month, not necessarily previous calendar month.
questions.solution: WITH monthly AS(SELECT strftime('%Y-%m',order_date) AS month,SUM(sales) AS sales FROM fact_sales GROUP BY month) SELECT month,sales,SUM(sales) OVER(ORDER BY month ROWS UNBOUNDED PRECEDING) AS running_sales FROM monthly ORDER BY month

questions.title: Monthly change & cumulative reports · Challenge 2
questions.prompt: Return month,sales,previous_sales,change_pct for observed months. Compare to previous observed month; percentage rounded to 2 decimals, NULL with no/nonzero denominator. Sort by month.
questions.rationale: Monthly cumulative sales transfer to percentage change; comparison is previous observed month, not necessarily previous calendar month.
questions.solution: WITH monthly AS(SELECT strftime('%Y-%m',order_date) AS month,SUM(sales) AS sales FROM fact_sales GROUP BY month),compared AS(SELECT *,LAG(sales) OVER(ORDER BY month) AS previous_sales FROM monthly) SELECT month,sales,previous_sales,ROUND(100.0*(sales-previous_sales)/NULLIF(previous_sales,0),2) AS change_pct FROM compared ORDER BY month

questions.title: Reconcile extraction & Bronze ingestion · Challenge 1
questions.prompt: Return source_name,expected_rows,landed_rows,difference (landed minus expected) for CRM and ERP using load_manifest and the raw tables.
questions.rationale: Extraction row-count reconciliation transfers to invalid-key evidence; a matching total alone does not establish mapping correctness.
questions.solution: WITH landed AS(SELECT 'CRM' AS source_name,COUNT(*) AS landed_rows FROM crm_people UNION ALL SELECT 'ERP',COUNT(*) FROM erp_people) SELECT m.source_name,m.expected_rows,l.landed_rows,l.landed_rows-m.expected_rows AS difference FROM load_manifest m JOIN landed l USING(source_name)

questions.title: Reconcile extraction & Bronze ingestion · Challenge 2
questions.difficultyWhy: Reviewed (rubric said warmup, score 0.5): Missing-or-blank check needs TRIM and NULL reasoning, beyond a warm-up.
questions.prompt: Return source_row and customer_id for CRM records with a missing or whitespace-only customer key. Do not modify Bronze.
questions.rationale: Extraction row-count reconciliation transfers to invalid-key evidence; a matching total alone does not establish mapping correctness.
questions.solution: SELECT source_row,customer_id FROM crm_people WHERE customer_id IS NULL OR TRIM(customer_id)=''

questions.title: Integrate CRM + ERP with source authority · Challenge 1
questions.prompt: Return customer_id,name,gender,country,birth_date using the integration contract in Understand. Use latest normalized CRM keys, CRM-first gender, ERP fallback, mapped country, and valid nonfuture birth date.
questions.rationale: Source-authority integration transfers to grouped resolved values; explicit CRM precedence and fallback remain necessary context.
questions.solution: WITH crm AS(WITH ranked AS (SELECT *,ROW_NUMBER() OVER(PARTITION BY TRIM(customer_id) ORDER BY updated_at DESC,source_row DESC) AS rn FROM crm_people WHERE customer_id IS NOT NULL AND TRIM(customer_id)<>'') SELECT TRIM(customer_id) AS customer_id,TRIM(name) AS name,CASE UPPER(TRIM(gender)) WHEN 'F' THEN 'Female' WHEN 'M' THEN 'Male' ELSE NULL END AS crm_gender FROM ranked WHERE rn=1),erp AS(SELECT CASE WHEN SUBSTR(TRIM(erp_id),1,3)='NAS' THEN SUBSTR(TRIM(erp_id),4) ELSE TRIM(erp_id) END AS customer_id,CASE UPPER(TRIM(gender)) WHEN 'F' THEN 'Female' WHEN 'FEMALE' THEN 'Female' WHEN 'M' THEN 'Male' WHEN 'MALE' THEN 'Male' ELSE NULL END AS erp_gender,birth_date FROM erp_people),loc AS(SELECT REPLACE(TRIM(erp_id),'-','') AS customer_id,CASE UPPER(TRIM(country_code)) WHEN 'US' THEN 'United States' WHEN 'USA' THEN 'United States' WHEN 'GB' THEN 'United Kingdom' WHEN 'UK' THEN 'United Kingdom' WHEN 'IND' THEN 'India' ELSE 'Unknown' END AS country FROM erp_locations) SELECT c.customer_id,c.name,COALESCE(c.crm_gender,e.erp_gender,'Unknown') AS gender,COALESCE(l.country,'Unknown') AS country,CASE WHEN e.birth_date GLOB '[0-9][0-9][0-9][0-9]-[0-9][0-9]-[0-9][0-9]' AND date(e.birth_date,'+0 days')=e.birth_date AND e.birth_date<='2025-04-01' THEN e.birth_date ELSE NULL END AS birth_date FROM crm c LEFT JOIN erp e ON e.customer_id=c.customer_id LEFT JOIN loc l ON l.customer_id=c.customer_id

questions.title: Integrate CRM + ERP with source authority · Challenge 2
questions.prompt: Use the same integration contract; return gender and customer_count grouped by the resolved gender.
questions.rationale: Source-authority integration transfers to grouped resolved values; explicit CRM precedence and fallback remain necessary context.
