 SELECT c.shopper_id,c.session_no,c.cart_id,c.id AS checkout_id,c.occurred_at AS checkout_at,
        p.id AS purchase_id,p.occurred_at AS purchase_at
 FROM session_events c JOIN session_events p ON p.shopper_id=c.shopper_id AND p.session_no=c.session_no
 AND p.cart_id=c.cart_id AND p.event_type='purchase' AND (p.occurred_at>c.occurred_at OR (p.occurred_at=c.occurred_at AND p.id>c.id))
 WHERE c.event_type='checkout' AND EXISTS(
 SELECT 1 FROM session_events v WHERE v.shopper_id=c.shopper_id AND v.session_no=c.session_no
 AND v.cart_id=c.cart_id AND v.event_type='view' AND (c.occurred_at>v.occurred_at OR (c.occurred_at=v.occurred_at AND c.id>v.id)))
), converted AS (SELECT DISTINCT shopper_id,session_no FROM funnel_pairs)
SELECT s.channel,COUNT(*) AS sessions,COUNT(c.session_no) AS converted_sessions,
ROUND(100.0*COUNT(c.session_no)/COUNT(*),2) AS conversion_pct
FROM session_list s LEFT JOIN converted c ON c.shopper_id=s.shopper_id AND c.session_no=s.session_no
GROUP BY s.channel ORDER BY s.channel

questions.title: Build a replay-safe ledger load
questions.difficultyWhy: Resolve conflicting source versions, preserve newer target records and prove repeated execution is safe.
questions.prompt: Merge market_load_feed into market_ledger. For each external_id choose the highest source version, breaking ties by greatest feed id. Insert missing keys and replace a target only when the source version is at least its version. Return the entire final ledger.
questions.rationale: Implement an idempotent upsert that handles duplicate source versions and late stale records. Resolve conflicting source versions, preserve newer target records and prove repeated execution is safe.
edgeCases: Do not delete target-only or newer target rows. Z starts at version 9, amount 90 and must survive its stale feed record.
Order by external_id. Your complete script is tested twice on the same database to check that it is safe to rerun. This is checked with both the sample data and different data.
The feed is immutable; do not clear it or use a one-shot marker to bypass processing.
rejectedApproaches: Overwrites a newer target with a stale source version.
Works once but fails when the whole script is replayed.
Chooses the wrong source record at a tied version.
hints: Rank feed rows before UPSERT so conflicting versions have one deterministic winner.
Add a WHERE condition to DO UPDATE to protect newer target versions.

questions.title: Enforce the reservation boundary
questions.difficultyWhy: Filter invalid references and storage types before deduplicating, then enforce equivalent rules for future writes.
questions.prompt: Create safe_reservations with shopper_id, item_id and quantity. Load the latest valid feed row for each shopper/item pair, then return the loaded rows. Valid input has existing shopper and item keys and an integer-stored quantity from 1 through 5.
questions.rationale: Separate staging cleanup from durable relational and domain constraints. Filter invalid references and storage types before deduplicating, then enforce equivalent rules for future writes.
edgeCases: Filter invalid feed rows before choosing greatest feed id per pair. A later invalid row must not suppress an earlier valid one.
The target must reject NULL keys, orphan keys, duplicate pairs, NULL quantity, fractional quantity and quantities outside 1–5; valid new rows must remain insertable.
Use a composite primary key, NOT NULL, foreign keys and a quantity CHECK including typeof(quantity). Order by shopper_id,item_id.
rejectedApproaches: Produces correct initial rows but accepts invalid future quantities.
Omits foreign keys: future orphan reservations succeed.
Loads the oldest valid row instead of the latest.
hints: Rank only rows that already passed type, range and parent-existence checks.
SQLite type affinity alone does not guarantee an integer; combine NOT NULL and a domain CHECK.
questions.solution:
CREATE TABLE safe_reservations(
shopper_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES shoppers(id),item_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES catalog_items(id),
quantity INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK(typeof(quantity)='integer' AND quantity BETWEEN 1 AND 5),
PRIMARY KEY(shopper_id,item_id));INSERT INTO safe_reservations WITH eligible AS (
SELECT f.*,ROW_NUMBER() OVER(PARTITION BY shopper_id,item_id ORDER BY f.id DESC) AS rn
FROM market_reservation_feed f WHERE typeof(quantity)='integer' AND quantity BETWEEN 1 AND 5
AND EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM shoppers s WHERE s.id=f.shopper_id)
AND EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM catalog_items c WHERE c.id=f.item_id))
SELECT shopper_id,item_id,quantity FROM eligible WHERE rn=1;
SELECT shopper_id,item_id,quantity FROM safe_reservations ORDER BY shopper_id,item_id

questions.title: Recover a failed stock allocation
questions.difficultyWhy: Recover both stock and audit effects of a rejected batch, preserve history and apply a valid batch atomically.
questions.prompt: The rejected batch cannot fit available stock: its item 2 request exceeds availability. Demonstrate recovery from a provisional reservation of 2 units of item 1 and a rejected audit entry, then apply only the accepted batch. Return item_id, available and reserved from the final stock table.
questions.rationale: Verify recovery by the final state of all affected tables, not transaction keywords. Recover both stock and audit effects of a rejected batch, preserve history and apply a valid batch atomically.
edgeCases: Use a savepoint to undo the provisional stock and audit work, then commit the accepted batch. Your answer is checked by looking at the resulting tables, without requiring particular SQL keywords.
Every stock row starts with available=capacity and reserved=0. Preserve all capacities and the historical audit row (units=5).
End with one accepted audit row whose units equal the accepted feed total, no rejected audit row, and each stock balance adjusted exactly once for its accepted quantity. Order by item_id.
rejectedApproaches: Commits the rejected provisional stock and audit changes.
Returns correct stock but leaves a rejected audit artifact.
hints: A rollback to the savepoint must undo both provisional table changes.
Drive the accepted update and audit total from the feed, including items added by changed data.

questions.title: Measure co-purchased product pairs
questions.difficultyWhy: Self-join a bridge table while eliminating self-pairs, mirrored pairs and quantity weighting.
questions.prompt: Find unordered pairs of distinct products appearing together in delivered orders. Return the smaller item id as item_a, the larger as item_b, and the number of shared orders.
questions.rationale: Count distinct baskets supporting each unordered product combination. Self-join a bridge table while eliminating self-pairs, mirrored pairs and quantity weighting.
edgeCases: Count an order once regardless of item quantities. The order_lines primary key is (order_id,item_id).
Only delivered orders qualify. Order by shared_orders descending, then item_a,item_b ascending.
rejectedApproaches: Counts both mirrored versions of each pair.
hints: Join order_lines to itself on order_id.
Use a.item_id < b.item_id to remove both self-pairs and mirrored combinations.
questions.solution:
SELECT a.item_id AS item_a,b.item_id AS item_b,COUNT(*) AS shared_orders
FROM order_lines a JOIN order_lines b ON b.order_id=a.order_id AND a.item_id<b.item_id
JOIN sales_orders o ON o.id=a.order_id WHERE o.status='delivered'
GROUP BY a.item_id,b.item_id ORDER BY shared_orders DESC,item_a,item_b

questions.title: Find shoppers in every category
questions.difficultyWhy: Express relational division over a dynamic category universe, respecting delivered-order membership.
questions.prompt: Return shoppers who bought at least one item from every distinct category currently in catalog_items, considering only delivered orders.
questions.rationale: Find entities related to every member of a changing required set. Express relational division over a dynamic category universe, respecting delivered-order membership.
edgeCases: Derive the required category set from the catalog; do not hardcode four categories or named categories.
Multiple products and orders in one category count only once. Include every qualifying shopper and order by shopper_id.
This exercise adds two illustrative orders to the standard Retail data; previews include them.
rejectedApproaches: Lets a cancelled order satisfy a required category.
Hardcodes the initial number of categories.
hints: Read double NOT EXISTS as “there is no required category missing from this shopper”.
An alternative is counting distinct purchased categories against the catalog category count.
questions.solution:
SELECT s.id AS shopper_id,s.name FROM shoppers s WHERE NOT EXISTS(
 SELECT 1 FROM catalog_items c WHERE NOT EXISTS(
 SELECT 1 FROM sales_orders o JOIN order_lines l ON l.order_id=o.id JOIN catalog_items bought ON bought.id=l.item_id
 WHERE o.shopper_id=s.id AND o.status='delivered' AND bought.category=c.category)) ORDER BY shopper_id

questions.title: Compare category audience overlap
questions.difficultyWhy: Reduce the bridge to shopper/category membership before computing set intersections and unions.
questions.prompt: For each alphabetically ordered pair of categories sharing at least one delivered-order shopper, return shared_buyers, union_buyers and jaccard = shared / union rounded to three decimals.
questions.rationale: Compute Jaccard overlap without inflating membership by line-item or repeat-order counts. Reduce the bridge to shopper/category membership before computing set intersections and unions.
edgeCases: A shopper belongs to a category once, regardless of repeat orders or quantities. Include only pairs with shared buyers.
Use category_a < category_b. Order by category_a,category_b.
rejectedApproaches: Lets repeat purchases multiply memberships and intersections.
Double-counts shared shoppers in the union.
hints: Build DISTINCT shopper_id/category membership first.
The union size is buyers(A) + buyers(B) − shared buyers.
questions.solution:
WITH membership AS (
SELECT DISTINCT o.shopper_id,c.category FROM sales_orders o JOIN order_lines l ON l.order_id=o.id
JOIN catalog_items c ON c.id=l.item_id WHERE o.status='delivered'
), totals AS (SELECT category,COUNT(*) AS buyers FROM membership GROUP BY category), intersections AS (
SELECT a.category AS category_a,b.category AS category_b,COUNT(*) AS shared_buyers
FROM membership a JOIN membership b ON b.shopper_id=a.shopper_id AND a.category<b.category GROUP BY a.category,b.category)
SELECT i.category_a,i.category_b,i.shared_buyers,ta.buyers+tb.buyers-i.shared_buyers AS union_buyers,
ROUND(1.0*i.shared_buyers/(ta.buyers+tb.buyers-i.shared_buyers),3) AS jaccard
FROM intersections i JOIN totals ta ON ta.category=i.category_a JOIN totals tb ON tb.category=i.category_b
ORDER BY i.category_a,i.category_b

questions.title: Parse malformed product codes
questions.difficultyWhy: Validate the entire token before extracting typed fields; CAST alone accepts malformed numeric prefixes.
questions.prompt: Normalize raw_code by trimming ASCII spaces and uppercasing it. Keep only codes of the exact form HM-DDDD-AA, where DDDD is four ASCII digits representing 1–9999 and AA is two ASCII letters. Return import_id, integer item_number and uppercase region.
questions.rationale: Normalize and validate a fixed-format identifier before parsing it. Validate the entire token before extracting typed fields; CAST alone accepts malformed numeric prefixes.
edgeCases: Reject NULL, 0000, extra characters, internal spaces and malformed delimiters. Order by import_id.
Region is any pair of ASCII letters, not a lookup against a country list.
rejectedApproaches: Accepts malformed digits because CAST returns a numeric prefix.
Rejects valid lowercase import codes instead of normalizing them.
hints: Check exact length and delimiter positions before casting.
NOT GLOB with a negated character class rejects a non-digit anywhere in a substring.
questions.solution:
WITH normalized AS (SELECT id,UPPER(TRIM(raw_code)) AS code FROM market_raw_import)
SELECT id AS import_id,CAST(SUBSTR(code,4,4) AS INTEGER) AS item_number,SUBSTR(code,9,2) AS region
FROM normalized WHERE LENGTH(code)=10 AND SUBSTR(code,1,3)='HM-' AND SUBSTR(code,8,1)='-'
AND SUBSTR(code,4,4) NOT GLOB '*[^0-9]*' AND CAST(SUBSTR(code,4,4) AS INTEGER)>0
AND SUBSTR(code,9,2) NOT GLOB '*[^A-Z]*' ORDER BY import_id

questions.title: Normalize contact import collisions
questions.difficultyWhy: Apply an explicit normalization and validity contract before grouping, without collapsing meaningful aliases.
questions.prompt: Find duplicate valid emails after lowercasing and trimming outer ASCII spaces, tabs, carriage returns and line feeds. Return normalized_email, source_rows and the smallest source id as first_id.
questions.rationale: Find normalized duplicate contacts while excluding malformed identifiers. Apply an explicit normalization and validity contract before grouping, without collapsing meaningful aliases.
edgeCases: For this exercise only: exactly one @; a nonempty local part; domain has a dot that is neither its first nor last character; no consecutive domain dots; no ASCII space, tab, CR or LF anywhere after trimming.
This is a deliberately limited import rule, not full email-standard validation. Keep plus aliases distinct; do not remove dots or plus suffixes.
Return only groups with more than one valid source row, ordered by normalized_email.
rejectedApproaches: Leaves tabs and line breaks around otherwise matching addresses.
Allows multiple @ symbols and groups malformed addresses.
hints: TRIM can take an explicit character set built with char(9), char(10), char(13) and space.
Count @ characters using the length difference before and after REPLACE.
questions.solution:
WITH normalized AS (
SELECT id,LOWER(TRIM(raw_email,char(9)||char(10)||char(13)||' ')) AS email FROM market_raw_import
), split AS (SELECT *,SUBSTR(email,INSTR(email,'@')+1) AS domain FROM normalized), valid AS (
SELECT * FROM split WHERE LENGTH(email)-LENGTH(REPLACE(email,'@',''))=1 AND INSTR(email,'@')>1
AND INSTR(domain,'.')>1 AND SUBSTR(domain,-1)<>'.' AND INSTR(domain,'..')=0
AND INSTR(email,' ')=0 AND INSTR(email,char(9))=0 AND INSTR(email,char(10))=0 AND INSTR(email,char(13))=0)
SELECT email AS normalized_email,COUNT(*) AS source_rows,MIN(id) AS first_id FROM valid
GROUP BY email HAVING COUNT(*)>1 ORDER BY normalized_email

questions.title: Parse money into exact integer cents
questions.difficultyWhy: Validate sign, decimal grammar and digit limits, then compute cents without permissive casts or floating-point rounding.
questions.prompt: For every import row, parse raw_amount into cents or NULL and label status valid or invalid. Trim outer ASCII spaces. Accept an optional leading + or -, one to six ASCII whole-number digits, and optionally a decimal point followed by one or two ASCII digits.
questions.rationale: Turn validated decimal text into exact integer minor units. Validate sign, decimal grammar and digit limits, then compute cents without permissive casts or floating-point rounding.
edgeCases: Leading zeros count toward the six-digit limit. Signed zero is valid. Missing whole digits, a trailing dot, exponents, separators, currency symbols and NULL are invalid.
Use integer cents: 19.99 is 1999 and -0.29 is -29. No floating-point tolerance is intended. Return every row ordered by import_id.
rejectedApproaches: Treats permissive casts as validation and uses floating-point money.
Accepts a whole-number part beyond the stated digit limit.
hints: Remove one optional sign, then split the unsigned body at its first dot.
Validate both digit substrings before casting. Pad the fraction to two places, then combine whole*100 + fraction.
questions.solution:
WITH stripped AS (SELECT id,TRIM(raw_amount) AS raw FROM market_raw_import),
unsigned AS (SELECT *,CASE WHEN SUBSTR(raw,1,1) IN ('+','-') THEN SUBSTR(raw,2) ELSE raw END AS body,
CASE WHEN SUBSTR(raw,1,1)='-' THEN -1 ELSE 1 END AS sign FROM stripped),
parts AS (SELECT *,CASE WHEN INSTR(body,'.')=0 THEN body ELSE SUBSTR(body,1,INSTR(body,'.')-1) END AS whole,
CASE WHEN INSTR(body,'.')=0 THEN '' ELSE SUBSTR(body,INSTR(body,'.')+1) END AS fraction FROM unsigned),
checked AS (SELECT *,CASE WHEN LENGTH(whole) BETWEEN 1 AND 6 AND whole NOT GLOB '*[^0-9]*'
AND (INSTR(body,'.')=0 OR (LENGTH(fraction) BETWEEN 1 AND 2 AND fraction NOT GLOB '*[^0-9]*')) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS valid FROM parts)
SELECT id AS import_id,CASE WHEN valid=1 THEN sign*(CAST(whole AS INTEGER)*100+CAST(SUBSTR(fraction||'00',1,2) AS INTEGER)) END AS cents,
CASE WHEN valid=1 THEN 'valid' ELSE 'invalid' END AS status FROM checked ORDER BY import_id

questions.title: Checkout review 1: establish the baseline
questions.difficultyWhy: Aggregate at session grain, assign cross-midnight sessions to their start day, and distinguish sessions from shoppers.
questions.prompt: Retail is investigating checkout reliability. First build a daily session baseline: session_date, sessions, distinct shoppers and returning_sessions. A returning session is any session numbered greater than 1 for that shopper in this observation dataset.
questions.rationale: Establish the daily population before interpreting checkout performance. Aggregate at session grain, assign cross-midnight sessions to their start day, and distinguish sessions from shoppers.
edgeCases: This stage starts from the original event tables in a fresh database. Recompute any intermediate results; nothing is carried over from earlier stages.
Deduplicate globally by event_key, keeping the smallest id; a retry may have a conflicting payload.
Use (occurred_at, id) as the total event order; equal timestamps follow id order. All times are UTC.

A shopper starts a session at the first canonical event or after a gap strictly greater than 30 minutes from their previous canonical event. Exactly 30 minutes stays in the same session; midnight alone does not split it.
Session numbers start at 1 per shopper and include every event type, including heartbeat and purchase-only sessions.
Assign the whole session to the UTC date of its first event, even if it crosses midnight. Order by session_date.
rejectedApproaches: Labels every first observed session as returning.
hints: Build one row per shopper/session before grouping by start date.
Returning means a later session in this dataset, not whether the shopper registered earlier.

questions.title: Checkout review 2: locate funnel drop-off
questions.difficultyWhy: Build nested ordered-funnel populations before calculating stage-to-stage losses.
questions.prompt: Continue the checkout review by returning three rows: view, checkout and purchase. Count sessions reaching each ordered stage. Return stage_no (1–3), stage, sessions and dropoff from the preceding stage.
questions.rationale: Diagnose the funnel stage at which eligible sessions stop progressing. Build nested ordered-funnel populations before calculating stage-to-stage losses.
edgeCases: This stage starts from the original event tables in a fresh database. Recompute any intermediate results; nothing is carried over from earlier stages.
Deduplicate globally by event_key, keeping the smallest id; a retry may have a conflicting payload.
Use (occurred_at, id) as the total event order; equal timestamps follow id order. All times are UTC.

A shopper starts a session at the first canonical event or after a gap strictly greater than 30 minutes from their previous canonical event. Exactly 30 minutes stays in the same session; midnight alone does not split it.
Session numbers start at 1 per shopper and include every event type, including heartbeat and purchase-only sessions.

A converted session has a view → checkout → purchase in that order, with all three events for the same shopper/cart within the session. Use the total event order. No extra view-to-purchase time limit applies.
View requires any view. Checkout requires an earlier same-cart view. Purchase requires the full ordered funnel. Count a session at most once per stage.
dropoff is previous-stage sessions minus current-stage sessions; use NULL for view. Order by stage_no.
rejectedApproaches: Accepts a view that occurs after checkout in the conversion path.
Reverses stage losses into negative values.
hints: Produce separate one-row-per-session sets for each reached stage.
Union their counts into three rows, then use LAG to calculate losses.
questions.solution:
WITH ranked_events AS (
 SELECT *,ROW_NUMBER() OVER(PARTITION BY event_key ORDER BY id) AS retry_rank
 FROM market_web_events
), events AS (SELECT * FROM ranked_events WHERE retry_rank=1), previous_events AS (
 SELECT *,LAG(occurred_at) OVER(PARTITION BY shopper_id ORDER BY occurred_at,id) AS previous_at FROM events
), marked AS (
 SELECT *,CASE WHEN previous_at IS NULL OR unixepoch(occurred_at)-unixepoch(previous_at)>1800 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS starts_session FROM previous_events
), session_events AS (
 SELECT *,SUM(starts_session) OVER(PARTITION BY shopper_id ORDER BY occurred_at,id ROWS UNBOUNDED PRECEDING) AS session_no FROM marked
), positioned AS (
 SELECT *,ROW_NUMBER() OVER(PARTITION BY shopper_id,session_no ORDER BY occurred_at,id) AS position FROM session_events
), session_list AS (
 SELECT shopper_id,session_no,occurred_at AS started_at,channel FROM positioned WHERE position=1
), funnel_pairs AS (
 SELECT c.shopper_id,c.session_no,c.cart_id,c.id AS checkout_id,c.occurred_at AS checkout_at,
        p.id AS purchase_id,p.occurred_at AS purchase_at
 FROM session_events c JOIN session_events p ON p.shopper_id=c.shopper_id AND p.session_no=c.session_no
 AND p.cart_id=c.cart_id AND p.event_type='purchase' AND (p.occurred_at>c.occurred_at OR (p.occurred_at=c.occurred_at AND p.id>c.id))
 WHERE c.event_type='checkout' AND EXISTS(
 SELECT 1 FROM session_events v WHERE v.shopper_id=c.shopper_id AND v.session_no=c.session_no
 AND v.cart_id=c.cart_id AND v.event_type='view' AND (c.occurred_at>v.occurred_at OR (c.occurred_at=v.occurred_at AND c.id>v.id)))
), converted AS (SELECT DISTINCT shopper_id,session_no FROM funnel_pairs), viewed AS (
SELECT DISTINCT shopper_id,session_no FROM session_events WHERE event_type='view'), checked_out AS (
SELECT DISTINCT c.shopper_id,c.session_no FROM session_events c WHERE c.event_type='checkout' AND EXISTS(
SELECT 1 FROM session_events v WHERE v.shopper_id=c.shopper_id AND v.session_no=c.session_no AND v.cart_id=c.cart_id AND v.event_type='view' AND (c.occurred_at>v.occurred_at OR (c.occurred_at=v.occurred_at AND c.id>v.id)))),
stages AS (SELECT 1 AS stage_no,'view' AS stage,COUNT(*) AS sessions FROM viewed
UNION ALL SELECT 2,'checkout',COUNT(*) FROM checked_out UNION ALL SELECT 3,'purchase',COUNT(*) FROM converted)
SELECT stage_no,stage,sessions,LAG(sessions) OVER(ORDER BY stage_no)-sessions AS dropoff FROM stages ORDER BY stage_no

questions.title: Checkout review 3: measure the delay tail
questions.difficultyWhy: Choose a deterministic successful attempt per session and calculate a discrete percentile at the correct grain.
questions.prompt: For each first-touch channel with converted sessions, report converted_sessions, avg_seconds from checkout to purchase rounded to two decimals, and the nearest-rank p90_seconds.
questions.rationale: Measure checkout latency without weighting sessions by repeated attempts. Choose a deterministic successful attempt per session and calculate a discrete percentile at the correct grain.
edgeCases: This stage starts from the original event tables in a fresh database. Recompute any intermediate results; nothing is carried over from earlier stages.
Deduplicate globally by event_key, keeping the smallest id; a retry may have a conflicting payload.
Use (occurred_at, id) as the total event order; equal timestamps follow id order. All times are UTC.

A shopper starts a session at the first canonical event or after a gap strictly greater than 30 minutes from their previous canonical event. Exactly 30 minutes stays in the same session; midnight alone does not split it.
Session numbers start at 1 per shopper and include every event type, including heartbeat and purchase-only sessions.

A converted session has a view → checkout → purchase in that order, with all three events for the same shopper/cart within the session. Use the total event order. No extra view-to-purchase time limit applies.
Within a session choose the earliest qualifying purchase in total event order. For that purchase choose the latest preceding same-cart checkout that has an earlier same-cart view in the session.

Measure elapsed seconds from that checkout to purchase. Attribute to the session’s first-event channel. For n sessions, nearest-rank p90 is the sorted value at ceil(0.9*n), one-based. Include no unconverted sessions; order by channel.
rejectedApproaches: Uses the first rather than the last eligible checkout before the chosen purchase.
Measures from session start instead of the selected checkout.
Reports the fastest session as the 90th percentile.
hints: Rank qualifying checkout/purchase pairs before computing any channel averages.
Use ROW_NUMBER and COUNT per channel; the integer expression (9*n+9)/10 computes the nearest-rank position.
questions.solution:
WITH ranked_events AS (
 SELECT *,ROW_NUMBER() OVER(PARTITION BY event_key ORDER BY id) AS retry_rank
 FROM market_web_events
), events AS (SELECT * FROM ranked_events WHERE retry_rank=1), previous_events AS (
 SELECT *,LAG(occurred_at) OVER(PARTITION BY shopper_id ORDER BY occurred_at,id) AS previous_at FROM events
), marked AS (
 SELECT *,CASE WHEN previous_at IS NULL OR unixepoch(occurred_at)-unixepoch(previous_at)>1800 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS starts_session FROM previous_events
), session_events AS (
 SELECT *,SUM(starts_session) OVER(PARTITION BY shopper_id ORDER BY occurred_at,id ROWS UNBOUNDED PRECEDING) AS session_no FROM marked
), positioned AS (
 SELECT *,ROW_NUMBER() OVER(PARTITION BY shopper_id,session_no ORDER BY occurred_at,id) AS position FROM session_events
), session_list AS (
 SELECT shopper_id,session_no,occurred_at AS started_at,channel FROM positioned WHERE position=1
), funnel_pairs AS (
 SELECT c.shopper_id,c.session_no,c.cart_id,c.id AS checkout_id,c.occurred_at AS checkout_at,
        p.id AS purchase_id,p.occurred_at AS purchase_at
 FROM session_events c JOIN session_events p ON p.shopper_id=c.shopper_id AND p.session_no=c.session_no
 AND p.cart_id=c.cart_id AND p.event_type='purchase' AND (p.occurred_at>c.occurred_at OR (p.occurred_at=c.occurred_at AND p.id>c.id))
 WHERE c.event_type='checkout' AND EXISTS(
 SELECT 1 FROM session_events v WHERE v.shopper_id=c.shopper_id AND v.session_no=c.session_no
 AND v.cart_id=c.cart_id AND v.event_type='view' AND (c.occurred_at>v.occurred_at OR (c.occurred_at=v.occurred_at AND c.id>v.id)))
), converted AS (SELECT DISTINCT shopper_id,session_no FROM funnel_pairs), chosen AS (
SELECT *,ROW_NUMBER() OVER(PARTITION BY shopper_id,session_no ORDER BY purchase_at,purchase_id,checkout_at DESC,checkout_id DESC) AS rn FROM funnel_pairs),
times AS (SELECT s.channel,ch.shopper_id,ch.session_no,unixepoch(ch.purchase_at)-unixepoch(ch.checkout_at) AS seconds
FROM chosen ch JOIN session_list s ON s.shopper_id=ch.shopper_id AND s.session_no=ch.session_no WHERE ch.rn=1),
ranked AS (SELECT *,ROW_NUMBER() OVER(PARTITION BY channel ORDER BY seconds,shopper_id,session_no) AS rank,
COUNT(*) OVER(PARTITION BY channel) AS n FROM times)
SELECT channel,COUNT(*) AS converted_sessions,ROUND(AVG(seconds),2) AS avg_seconds,
MAX(CASE WHEN rank=(9*n+9)/10 THEN seconds END) AS p90_seconds FROM ranked GROUP BY channel ORDER BY channel

questions.title: Checkout review 4: find later recoveries
questions.difficultyWhy: Link abandoned sessions to a later same-cart purchase within a bounded window without multiplying attempts.
questions.prompt: An abandoned session contains checkout but no full ordered conversion. Find abandoned sessions with a same-cart purchase in a strictly later session within 24 hours of a checkout in the abandoned session. Return shopper_id, abandoned_session, recovery_session and recovery_minutes.
questions.rationale: Distinguish same-session conversion from later recovery. Link abandoned sessions to a later same-cart purchase within a bounded window without multiplying attempts.
edgeCases: This stage starts from the original event tables in a fresh database. Recompute any intermediate results; nothing is carried over from earlier stages.
Deduplicate globally by event_key, keeping the smallest id; a retry may have a conflicting payload.
Use (occurred_at, id) as the total event order; equal timestamps follow id order. All times are UTC.

A shopper starts a session at the first canonical event or after a gap strictly greater than 30 minutes from their previous canonical event. Exactly 30 minutes stays in the same session; midnight alone does not split it.
Session numbers start at 1 per shopper and include every event type, including heartbeat and purchase-only sessions.

A converted session has a view → checkout → purchase in that order, with all three events for the same shopper/cart within the session. Use the total event order. No extra view-to-purchase time limit applies.
A recovery needs a purchase only; the later session need not repeat the view/checkout funnel. Match shopper and cart. The 24-hour bound is inclusive.

Choose the earliest qualifying later purchase per abandoned session, then the latest qualifying checkout for that purchase. Return one row per recovered abandoned session, rounded minutes to two decimals, ordered by shopper_id,abandoned_session.
rejectedApproaches: Calls a same-session unordered purchase a later recovery.
Uses a 12-hour recovery window instead of 24 hours.
hints: Derive abandoned session identities before joining checkout and later purchase events.
Rank recovery candidates per abandoned session to retain one earliest recovery.
questions.solution:
WITH ranked_events AS (
 SELECT *,ROW_NUMBER() OVER(PARTITION BY event_key ORDER BY id) AS retry_rank
 FROM market_web_events
), events AS (SELECT * FROM ranked_events WHERE retry_rank=1), previous_events AS (
 SELECT *,LAG(occurred_at) OVER(PARTITION BY shopper_id ORDER BY occurred_at,id) AS previous_at FROM events
), marked AS (
 SELECT *,CASE WHEN previous_at IS NULL OR unixepoch(occurred_at)-unixepoch(previous_at)>1800 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS starts_session FROM previous_events
), session_events AS (
 SELECT *,SUM(starts_session) OVER(PARTITION BY shopper_id ORDER BY occurred_at,id ROWS UNBOUNDED PRECEDING) AS session_no FROM marked
), positioned AS (
 SELECT *,ROW_NUMBER() OVER(PARTITION BY shopper_id,session_no ORDER BY occurred_at,id) AS position FROM session_events
), session_list AS (
 SELECT shopper_id,session_no,occurred_at AS started_at,channel FROM positioned WHERE position=1
), funnel_pairs AS (
 SELECT c.shopper_id,c.session_no,c.cart_id,c.id AS checkout_id,c.occurred_at AS checkout_at,
        p.id AS purchase_id,p.occurred_at AS purchase_at
 FROM session_events c JOIN session_events p ON p.shopper_id=c.shopper_id AND p.session_no=c.session_no
 AND p.cart_id=c.cart_id AND p.event_type='purchase' AND (p.occurred_at>c.occurred_at OR (p.occurred_at=c.occurred_at AND p.id>c.id))
 WHERE c.event_type='checkout' AND EXISTS(
 SELECT 1 FROM session_events v WHERE v.shopper_id=c.shopper_id AND v.session_no=c.session_no
 AND v.cart_id=c.cart_id AND v.event_type='view' AND (c.occurred_at>v.occurred_at OR (c.occurred_at=v.occurred_at AND c.id>v.id)))
), converted AS (SELECT DISTINCT shopper_id,session_no FROM funnel_pairs), abandoned AS (
SELECT DISTINCT c.shopper_id,c.session_no FROM session_events c WHERE c.event_type='checkout'
AND NOT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM converted v WHERE v.shopper_id=c.shopper_id AND v.session_no=c.session_no)),
recovery_candidates AS (
SELECT c.shopper_id,c.session_no AS abandoned_session,p.session_no AS recovery_session,
unixepoch(p.occurred_at)-unixepoch(c.occurred_at) AS seconds,
ROW_NUMBER() OVER(PARTITION BY c.shopper_id,c.session_no ORDER BY p.occurred_at,p.id,c.occurred_at DESC,c.id DESC) AS rn
FROM session_events c JOIN abandoned a ON a.shopper_id=c.shopper_id AND a.session_no=c.session_no
JOIN session_events p ON p.shopper_id=c.shopper_id AND p.cart_id=c.cart_id AND p.event_type='purchase'
AND p.session_no>c.session_no AND unixepoch(p.occurred_at)-unixepoch(c.occurred_at)<=86400
WHERE c.event_type='checkout'), recovered AS (SELECT * FROM recovery_candidates WHERE rn=1) SELECT shopper_id,abandoned_session,recovery_session,ROUND(seconds/60.0,2) AS recovery_minutes
FROM recovered ORDER BY shopper_id,abandoned_session

questions.title: Checkout review 5: prioritize channel fixes

A converted session has a view → checkout → purchase in that order, with all three events for the same shopper/cart within the session. Use the total event order. No extra view-to-purchase time limit applies.

Abandoned means the session has checkout but no full ordered conversion. Recovered means it has a same-cart purchase in a strictly later session within 24 hours (inclusive) of any checkout in the abandoned session.

questions.solution:
WITH ranked_events AS (
 SELECT *,ROW_NUMBER() OVER(PARTITION BY event_key ORDER BY id) AS retry_rank
 FROM market_web_events
), events AS (SELECT * FROM ranked_events WHERE retry_rank=1), previous_events AS (
 SELECT *,LAG(occurred_at) OVER(PARTITION BY shopper_id ORDER BY occurred_at,id) AS previous_at FROM events
), marked AS (
 SELECT *,CASE WHEN previous_at IS NULL OR unixepoch(occurred_at)-unixepoch(previous_at)>1800 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS starts_session FROM previous_events
), session_events AS (
 SELECT *,SUM(starts_session) OVER(PARTITION BY shopper_id ORDER BY occurred_at,id ROWS UNBOUNDED PRECEDING) AS session_no FROM marked
), positioned AS (
 SELECT *,ROW_NUMBER() OVER(PARTITION BY shopper_id,session_no ORDER BY occurred_at,id) AS position FROM session_events
), session_list AS (
 SELECT shopper_id,session_no,occurred_at AS started_at,channel FROM positioned WHERE position=1
), funnel_pairs AS (
 SELECT c.shopper_id,c.session_no,c.cart_id,c.id AS checkout_id,c.occurred_at AS checkout_at,
        p.id AS purchase_id,p.occurred_at AS purchase_at
 FROM session_events c JOIN session_events p ON p.shopper_id=c.shopper_id AND p.session_no=c.session_no
